That is, they were human beings among mankind, who ate and drank like people, and entered the markets for earning and trade. This was not harmful to them nor did it diminish them in any way, as the polytheists supposed in their saying: ﴿"What is this messenger that eats food and walks in the markets? Why was an angel not sent down to him to be a warner with him, or a treasure bestowed upon him, or a garden from which he might eat?" Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 21, verses 16–20:

Allah informs that He created the heavens and the earth with truth, meaning with justice and equity, ﴿so that He may recompense those who did evil for what they did and recompense those who did good with the best﴾ [An-Najm 53:31]. He did not create that in vain or as play, as He said: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾ [Sad 38:27].

* *

His saying, ﴿Had We intended to take a diversion, We would have taken it from Our presence, if We were ever to do [so]﴾. Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid: ﴿Had We intended to take a diversion, We would have taken it from Our presence﴾ means: from Our side. He says: "We did not create a Paradise, nor a Fire, nor death, nor resurrection, nor reckoning."

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and others said: ﴿a diversion﴾ (al-lahw) means "the woman" in the language of the people of Yemen.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: ﴿Had We intended to take a diversion, We would have taken it﴾ means: from the wide-eyed houris (al-hur al-'in).

'Ikrimah and al-Suddi said: the meaning of "diversion" here is "the child."

These and the preceding view are interrelated, and it is like His saying: ﴿Had Allah intended to take a son, He would have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills. Glory be to Him﴾ [Az-Zumar 39:4]. Thus He declared Himself free of taking a son absolutely, especially of what they say of falsehood and lies, such as taking 'Isa, or 'Uzayr, or the angels. ﴿Exalted is He above what they say, by a great elevation﴾ [Al-Isra 17:43].

* *

His saying, ﴿if We were ever to do [so]﴾. Qatadah, al-Suddi, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and Mughirah ibn Miqsam said: meaning, "We were not doing [it]."

Mujahid said: everything in the Qur'an with "in" (in) is a denial.

* *

His saying, ﴿Rather, We hurl the truth against falsehood, and it destroys it, and thereupon it departs. And for you is destruction from what you describe﴾. That is, We make the truth clear, and it crushes falsehood. Therefore He said: ﴿and thereupon it departs﴾, meaning it goes away and vanishes. ﴿And for you is destruction﴾, meaning: O you who claim that Allah has a son. ﴿From what you describe﴾, meaning: what you say and fabricate.

Then Allah informed about the servitude of the angels to Him and their constancy in obeying Him by night and day. He said: ﴿And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿are not arrogant toward His worship﴾, meaning they do not disdain it, as He said: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels near [to Him]. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them to Himself all together﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:172].

* *

His saying, ﴿And they do not grow weary﴾, meaning they do not tire and do not become bored.

﴿They exalt [Allah] night and day; they do not slacken﴾. So they are constant in action night and day, obedient in intention and deed, and able to do it, as He said: ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded﴾ [At-Tahrim 66:6].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn Abi Dulamah al-Baghdadi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' informed us, Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Safwan ibn Muhriz, from Hakim ibn Hizam, who said: "While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among his companions, he said to them: 'Do you hear what I hear?' They said: 'We hear nothing.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed I hear the creaking of the heaven, and it has the right to creak. There is no space the width of a palm in it except that there is an angel prostrating or standing upon it.'" Gharib, and they did not record it.

[Al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (3/201) and al-Tahawi in Mushkil al-Athar, no. 1134, narrated it through 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' with the same chain. It has a witness from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, recorded by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. 2312, who said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith."]

Then Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the route of Yazid ibn Zuray', from Sa'id, from Qatadah, as a mursal report.

Abu Ishaq [in H, F, A: "Muhammad ibn Ishaq," and the established reading is from al-Tabari 17/70], narrated from Hassan ibn Mukhariq, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, who said: "I sat with Ka'b al-Ahbar when I was a youth, and I said to him: 'Have you considered the saying of Allah [to the angels] [addition from F, A] ﴿They exalt [Allah] night and day; they do not slacken﴾?

So He said: ﴿Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honoured servants﴾, meaning: the angels are servants of Allah, honoured by Him, in lofty positions and exalted ranks, and they are in complete obedience to Him in word and deed.

﴿They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command﴾, meaning: they do not go ahead of Him with any matter, nor do they oppose Him in what He commands them, but they hasten to carry it out. And His knowledge encompasses them, so nothing about them is hidden from Him: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those with whom He is pleased﴾, it is like His saying: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255], and His saying: ﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He has permitted﴾ [Saba': 23], and other verses with the same meaning.

And whoever among them should say, "Indeed, I am a deity besides Him"﴾, meaning: whoever among them claims to be a god besides Allah, that is, along with Allah, ﴿that one We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: everyone who says that. How, then, is it fitting that other than Him be worshipped, or that anything else be associated with Him? ﴿Did they not see that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass﴾, that is, everything was connected, one part attached to another, piled up, one part above another at the beginning of things, ﴿then We separated them﴾, splitting this from that. This is why He said: ﴿And We made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?﴾, that is, while they witness creatures coming into being little by little, plainly before their eyes. Atiyyah al-Awfi said: "This [heaven] was a joined mass, not raining, so it rained; and this [earth] was a joined mass, not producing, so it produced."

* *

His words ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ mean that the origin of all living things is water.

He (ﷺ) said: "Everything was created from water."

* *

His words ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains﴾ mean mountains by which He anchored and established the earth and made it heavy, lest it sway with the people, that is, shake and tremble, so that they would find no stability on it. This is why He said: ﴿lest it sway with them﴾, that is, lest it sway with them.

* *

His words ﴿And We made in it broad roads as paths﴾ mean openings through the mountains, through which they travel roads from one region to another and from one climate to another, as is observed on earth. A mountain may stand as a barrier between one land and another, so Allah makes an opening in it, a gap, so that people may pass through it from here to there. This is why He said: ﴿that they may be guided﴾.

* *

* *

Then He said, drawing attention to some of His signs: ﴿And He it is who created the night and the day﴾, that is, this in its darkness and stillness, and that in its light and brightness; this lengthens at times and then shortens at others, and the reverse. ﴿And the sun and the moon﴾: this has a light specific to it, its own orbit, its own time, and a particular motion and course; and that has another light, another orbit, another course, and another measure. ﴿And each in an orbit is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40], that is, they revolve.

Ibn Abbas said: "They revolve as the spindle turns in the whorl." Mujahid likewise said: "The spindle turns only with the whorl, and the whorl only with the spindle; so too the stars, the sun and the moon: they revolve only through it, and it revolves only through them." As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He is the splitter of the dawn, and He made the night for rest and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 96].

He, may He be exalted, says, drawing attention to His complete power and His great sovereignty in creating things and in subduing all creatures: ﴿Have not those who disbelieve seen﴾, that is, those who deny His divinity and worship others alongside Him? Did they not know that Allah alone is the One who independently creates and solely directs affairs? How, then, is it fitting that other than Him be worshipped, or that anything else be associated with Him? ﴿Did they not see that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass﴾, that is, everything was connected, one part attached to another, piled up, one part above another at the beginning of things, ﴿then We separated them﴾, splitting this from that. He made the heavens seven and the earth seven, and He separated the lowest heaven from the earth by the air. The sky then rained and the earth brought forth plants. This is why He said: ﴿And We made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?﴾, that is, while they witness creatures coming into being little by little, plainly before their eyes. That is a proof of the existence of the Creator, the Doer, the Chooser, the One able to do whatever He wills. ~ "In everything there is a sign that points to His oneness..."

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from his father, from Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked, "Was the night before the day, or the day before the night?" He said: "Have you seen the heavens and the earth when they were a joined mass? Was there anything between them but darkness?" That is so that you may know that the night came before the day.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Abi Hamzah narrated to us, Hatim narrated to us, from Hamzah ibn Abi Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, that a man came to him asking about the heavens and the earth: ﴿that they were a joined mass, then We split them﴾? He said: "Go to that shaykh and ask him, then come and tell me what he said to you." So the man went to Ibn Abbas and asked him. Ibn Abbas said: "Yes, the heavens were a joined mass, not raining, and the earth was a joined mass, not producing plants. When He created inhabitants for the earth, He split this from that with rain, and split that from this with plants." The man returned to Ibn Umar and informed him. Ibn Umar said: "Now I know that Ibn Abbas has been given knowledge of the Qur'an. He is right; it was just so." Ibn Umar had also said: "I used to say, 'I do not like the boldness of Ibn Abbas in interpreting the Qur'an,' but now I know that he has indeed been given knowledge of the Qur'an."

Atiyyah al-Awfi said: "This [heaven] was a joined mass, not raining, so it rained; and this [earth] was a joined mass, not producing, so it produced."

Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid said: I asked Abu Salih al-Hanafi about His words: ﴿that the heavens and the earth were a joined mass, then We split them﴾. He said: "The heaven was one, and He split from it seven heavens; the earth was one, and He split from it seven earths."

Mujahid said the same and added: "The heaven and the earth had not been touching each other."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Rather, the heaven and the earth were stuck together. When He raised the heaven and brought the earth forth from it, that was their splitting which Allah mentioned in His Book." Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: "They were both one entity, then He separated them with this air."

* *

His words ﴿And We made from water every living thing﴾ mean that the origin of all living things is water.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Jamahir narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Bashir narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Abu Maymunah, from Abu Hurayrah, that he said: "O Prophet of Allah, when I see you my eye is delighted and my soul is content, so inform me about everything." He (ﷺ) said: "Everything was created from water."

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Maymunah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, when I see you my soul is content and my eye is delighted, so tell me about everything." He said: "Everything was created from water." I said: "Tell me of a deed which, if I do it, I will enter Paradise." He said: "Spread the greeting of peace, feed the food, uphold the ties of kinship, and pray at night when people are asleep, then you will enter Paradise in peace."

He also narrated it through Abd al-Samad, Affan and Bahz, from Hammam. Ahmad alone transmitted it. This chain is according to the conditions of the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, the two authentic collections of Bukhari and Muslim), except that Abu Maymunah is among the narrators of the Sunan collections, whose name is Sulaym, and al-Tirmidhi authenticates his narrations. Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah narrated it from Qatadah as a mursal report (one in which the Successor reports directly from the Prophet without naming the Companion), and Allah knows best.

* *

His words ﴿And We placed in the earth firm mountains﴾ mean mountains by which He anchored and established the earth and made it heavy, lest it sway with the people, that is, shake and tremble, so that they would find no stability on it. The earth is submerged in water except for a quarter, which is exposed to the air and the sun, so that its people may witness the sky and the stunning signs and wisdoms and proofs within it. This is why He said: ﴿lest it sway with them﴾, that is, lest it sway with them.

* *

His words ﴿And We made in it broad roads as paths﴾ mean openings through the mountains, through which they travel roads from one region to another and from one climate to another, as is observed on earth. A mountain may stand as a barrier between one land and another, so Allah makes an opening in it, a gap, so that people may pass through it from here to there. This is why He said: ﴿that they may be guided﴾.

* *

His words ﴿And We made the sky a canopy﴾ mean over the earth, and it is like a dome over it, as He said: ﴿And the sky We built with might, and indeed We are expanding it﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 47], and He said: ﴿By the sky and He who built it﴾ [ash-Shams: 5], and: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them, how We built it and adorned it, and it has no fissures?﴾ [Qaf: 6]. Building is the raising of a dome, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Islam is built upon five," meaning five pillars. This is only found in tents, as the Arabs know them.

﴿Protected﴾ means elevated and guarded from being reached. Mujahid said: "raised."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ash'ath, that is, Ibn Ishaq al-Qummi, from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, what is this sky?" He said: "A surging wave held back from you." This is a gharib (a report narrated by a single transmitter at some point in its chain) chain.

* *

His words ﴿Yet they turn away from its signs﴾ are like His words: ﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, yet they turn away from it﴾ [Yusuf: 105], that is, they do not reflect upon what Allah created in them of vast expanse, awesome height, the stars fixed and wandering that adorn them by night, and the sun by day, which traverses the whole sphere in a day and a night, moving to a limit whose extent none knows except the One who measured it, subjected it and set it in motion.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned in his book "Al-Tafakkur wa al-I'tibar" (Reflection and Contemplation) that one of the worshippers of the Children of Israel worshipped for thirty years, and whenever a man among them worshipped for thirty years, a cloud would shade him. This man saw nothing of what others used to see, so he complained of this to his mother. She said to him: "My son, perhaps you sinned during this period of your worship." He said: "No, by Allah, I know of nothing." She said: "Perhaps you had an evil intention?" He said: "No, nor did I intend anything." She said: "Perhaps you raised your gaze to the sky and then lowered it without reflection?" He said: "Yes, many times." She said: "From here you were brought low."

Then He said, drawing attention to some of His signs: ﴿And He it is who created the night and the day﴾, that is, this in its darkness and stillness, and that in its light and brightness; this lengthens at times and then shortens at others, and the reverse. ﴿And the sun and the moon﴾: this has a light specific to it, its own orbit, its own time, and a particular motion and course; and that has another light, another orbit, another course, and another measure. ﴿And each in an orbit is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40], that is, they revolve.

Ibn Abbas said: "They revolve as the spindle turns in the whorl." Mujahid likewise said: "The spindle turns only with the whorl, and the whorl only with the spindle; so too the stars, the sun and the moon: they revolve only through it, and it revolves only through them." As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿He is the splitter of the dawn, and He made the night for rest and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [al-An'am: 96].

God says: ﴿We did not grant immortality to any human before you﴾, meaning, O Muhammad, ﴿immortality﴾ in this world. Rather, ﴿everyone upon it will perish, but the Face of your Lord, Lord of Majesty and Honor, will remain﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 26, 27].

Some scholars who hold that al-Khadir (peace be upon him) died and is not alive until now have used this noble verse as evidence, because he is a human being, whether he was a saint, a prophet, or a messenger. God says: ﴿We did not grant immortality to any human before you﴾.

* *

His words ﴿So if you die, will they be the immortals?﴾ mean, O Muhammad, will they be the ones who live forever? That is, they hope to live after you. This will not happen. Rather, everyone is subject to annihilation. For this reason He says: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾. It is narrated from al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, that he recited and cited these two verses:

*Some men wished that I would die, but if I die, that is a path in which I am not unique.*

*So say to the one who seeks to oppose what has passed: prepare yourself for another like it, for it is as if it has already come.* [The two verses were mentioned by al-Bayhaqi in Manaqib al-Shafi'i (2/62) and al-Razi in Manaqib al-Shafi'i (p. 119).]

* *

His words ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial﴾ mean: We examine you with calamities at one time and with blessings at another, so that We may see who gives thanks and who disbelieves, and who is patient and who despairs. As Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And We test you﴾, he said: We try you with evil and good as a trial, with hardship and ease, health and sickness, wealth and poverty, the lawful and the unlawful, obedience and disobedience, guidance and misguidance.

* *

His words ﴿And to Us you will be returned﴾ mean: then We will recompense you for your deeds.

God says: ﴿We did not grant immortality to any human before you﴾, meaning, O Muhammad, ﴿immortality﴾ in this world. Rather, ﴿everyone upon it will perish, but the Face of your Lord, Lord of Majesty and Honor, will remain﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 26, 27].

*So say to the one who seeks to oppose what has passed: prepare yourself for another like it, for it is as if it has already come.* [The two verses were mentioned by al-Bayhaqi in Manaqib al-Shafi'i (2/62) and al-Razi in Manaqib al-Shafi'i (p. 119).]

* *

* *

His words ﴿And to Us you will be returned﴾ mean: then We will recompense you for your deeds.

Allah says to His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in mockery, [saying], "Is this the one who mentions your gods?"﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Quraysh, such as Abu Jahl and his likes. "They take you not except in mockery" means they ridicule you and belittle you. They say: "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" meaning: Is this the one who reviles your gods and makes foolish your minds? Allah says: ﴿And they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.﴾ That is, they disbelieve in Allah, and despite this they mock the Messenger of Allah, as He says in another verse: ﴿And when they see you, they take you not except in mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger? He would have almost led us away from our gods had we not remained steadfast to them." But they will know, when they see the punishment, who is further astray in way.﴾ [al-Furqan: 41, 42].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾, it is like His saying in another verse: ﴿And man has ever been hasty﴾ [al-Isra: 11], that is, in matters.

Mujahid said: Allah created Adam after everything, at the end of the day, from the day He created the creation. When the spirit gave life to his eyes, his tongue and his head, but it had not reached his lower part, he said: "My Lord, hasten the creation of me before the setting of the sun."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Alqamah ibn Waqqas al-Laythi informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The best day on which the sun has risen is Friday. On it Adam was created, on it he was admitted to Paradise, on it he was expelled from it, and on it the Hour will be established. And there is an hour on it in which no believer who is praying coincides with it and asks Allah for good except that He gives it to him," and he gathered his fingers, minimizing them. Abu Salamah said: Abdullah ibn Salam said: "I know that hour; it is the last hour of the day on Friday, and it is the one in which Allah created Adam." Allah the Most High said: ﴿Man was created of haste. I will show you My signs, so do not ask Me to hasten.﴾ [[Malik narrated in al-Muwatta (1/108) through Yazid ibn al-Hadi, from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, something similar without mention of the verse, and al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated its beginning, and Allah knows best.]]

The wisdom in mentioning the haste of man here is that when He mentioned those who mock the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, a desire for swift retribution against them arose in souls and hastened them, so Allah the Most High said: ﴿Man was created of haste﴾; because He, the Most High, gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him go. He delays and then hastens, and gives time and then does not postpone. Therefore He said: ﴿I will show you My signs﴾, that is, My vengeance, My judgment, and My power over those who disobey Me, ﴿so do not ask Me to hasten﴾.

Allah says to His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿And when those who disbelieve see you, they take you not except in mockery, [saying], "Is this the one who mentions your gods?"﴾ That is, the disbelievers of Quraysh, such as Abu Jahl and his likes. Therefore He said: ﴿I will show you My signs﴾, that is, My vengeance, My judgment, and My power over those who disobey Me, ﴿so do not ask Me to hasten﴾.

Ibn Kathir says of the polytheists that they also hasten the coming of the punishment upon them, out of denial, obstinacy, disbelief, stubbornness and considering it far-fetched. So He said: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If only those who disbelieved knew the time when they will not be able to avert from their faces the Fire, nor from their backs﴾. That is: if they were certain that it would befall them without doubt, they would not have hastened (it). ﴿And if only they knew the time when the punishment will envelop them from above them and from beneath their feet﴾ [Quran 39:16 ﴿They will have above them layers of Fire, and beneath them layers﴾], [Quran 7:41 ﴿They will have from Hell a bed, and above them coverings﴾]. And He said in this verse: ﴿when they will not be able to avert from their faces the Fire, nor from their backs﴾, and He said: ﴿Their garments will be of pitch, and the Fire will cover their faces﴾ [Quran 14:50]. So the punishment encompasses them from all their directions. ﴿Nor will they be helped﴾, that is, they will have no helper, as He said: ﴿And they will have no protector from Allah﴾ [Quran 13:34].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly﴾ [in the manuscript F: "suddenly, and it will confound them"], that is, "the Fire will come upon them suddenly," meaning unexpectedly, ﴿and it will confound them﴾, that is, it will terrify them, so they will submit to it bewildered, not knowing what to do. ﴿And they will not be able to repel it﴾, that is, they have no means to do so. ﴿Nor will they be reprieved﴾, that is, it will not be delayed from them for a single moment.

* *

Ibn Kathir said, consoling His Messenger (ﷺ) for what the polytheists inflicted on him of mockery and denial: ﴿And indeed, messengers before you were mocked, but those who ridiculed them were encompassed by that which they used to mock.﴾ That is, by the punishment whose occurrence they considered far-fetched, as He says: ﴿And messengers were certainly denied before you, but they patiently endured what they were denied and were harmed until Our victory reached them. And there is none to alter the words of Allah. And there has certainly reached you some information about the messengers.﴾ [Al-An'am: 34].

Then He mentioned His favor upon His servants in preserving them by night and day, and His guarding and protection of them with His eye that does not sleep. He said: ﴿Say, "Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?"﴾ That is, "Who substitutes for the Most Merciful with something else," as the poet said: [[This is Abu Nukhaylah Ya'mur ibn Hazn; the verse is in Lisan al-Arab under the root (f-s-q), and its first half is: "Dassathu lam ta'kul al-muraqqaqa" (She did not eat the thin bread).

Ibn Manzur, in Lisan al-Arab, interpreted his saying as though he thought "fustuq" (pistachio) was a kind of herb.]]

"A girl who has not worn the fine garment, and has not tasted from the herbs the pistachio..."

That is: she has not tasted pistachio in place of herbs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾ That is, they do not acknowledge His blessings upon them and His kindness toward them; rather, they turn away from His signs and His bounties. Then He said: ﴿Or do they have gods that can protect them from Us?﴾ This is a rhetorical question of denial, rebuke and reproach; that is, "Do they have gods other than Us that can protect and guard them? The matter is not as they imagine or as they claim." Therefore He said: ﴿They are unable to help themselves﴾ That is, these [gods] (added in the manuscripts) upon which they relied besides Allah are unable to help themselves.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Nor will they be accompanied by Us.﴾ Al-Awfi reported from Ibn Abbas regarding it: "They will not be granted protection (yujarun)." Qatadah said: "They will not be accompanied by good from Allah." Others said: "They will not be prevented (yumna'un)."

If your punishment of them exceeds their sins, the excess that remains will be exacted from you for them." The man began to weep before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and cry out. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "What is wrong with him? Does he not read the Book of God: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged in anything, and even if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾?" The man said: O Messenger of God, I find nothing better than parting from these, meaning his slaves. I call you to witness that they are all free.[Musnad (6/280).]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 21, verses 48–50:

It has already been pointed out that Allah, exalted is He, frequently mentions Musa (Moses) and Muhammad together, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them both, along with their Books. For this reason He said: ﴿And We indeed gave Musa and Harun the Furqan﴾. Mujahid said: it means the Book. Abu Salih said: the Torah. Qatadah said: the Torah, its lawful and its unlawful, and that by which Allah distinguished between truth and falsehood. Ibn Zayd said: it means the victory.

The summary of what has been said on this matter: the heavenly Books include the distinction between truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, error and right direction, the lawful and the unlawful, and that which produces light in the hearts, guidance, fear, turning back to Allah, and awe. For this reason He said: ﴿the Furqan, and a light and a reminder for the God-fearing﴾, i.e., a reminder [[added from manuscript f.]] and an admonition for them.

Then He described them, saying: ﴿those who fear their Lord in the unseen﴾, like His saying: ﴿Whoever feared the Most Merciful in the unseen and came with a heart turning back (to Him)﴾ [Qaf: 33], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who fear their Lord in the unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾ [al-Mulk: 12], ﴿and they, of the Hour, are apprehensive﴾, i.e., fearful and anxious.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And this is a blessed reminder which We have sent down﴾, meaning the Great Qur'an, to which falsehood does not come from before it or from behind it, a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy, ﴿Then are you to it deniers?﴾, i.e., will you deny it while it is in the utmost [[added from manuscript f.]] clarity and manifestness?

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 21, verses 51–56:

God, exalted is He, tells us about His intimate friend (khalil) Ibrahim, peace be upon him, that He gave him his guidance (rushd) beforehand, that is, from his youth: He inspired him with the truth and with the proof against his people, as He says: ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Ibrahim against his people﴾ [al-An'am 6:83]. As for what is related from him concerning his father placing him in a cave (sirb) while he was a suckling infant, and that he went out with him after some days, then looked at the stars and the created things, reflected upon them, and what many of the exegetes and others have narrated about this, most of it consists of reports from the Children of Israel (isra'iliyyat). Whatever of these agrees with the truth that is in our hands from the infallible (al-Ma'sum, the Prophet ﷺ), we accept it because it agrees with what is sound; whatever contradicts anything of that we reject; and whatever has neither agreement nor contradiction, we neither confirm nor deny it, but treat it as permissible to mention (wifqan). Many of the early scholars (salaf) permitted narrating this kind of report, but much of it has no benefit and no outcome that is useful in religion. Had there been any benefit in it returning to the responsible persons in their religion, this complete and comprehensive Sharia would have explained it. What we follow in this tafsir is to turn away from many of the Israelite reports, because they waste time, and because much of them contains falsehood that has been circulated among them, for they do not distinguish between their sound and their weak reports, as the memorizing and precise imams of this community have established.

The point here is that God, exalted is He, informed that He had given Ibrahim his guidance before that, that is, before that time. His words ﴿and We knew him well﴾ mean: he was worthy of that.

Then He said: ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these images to which you are devoted?"﴾ This is the guidance he was given from his youth: denouncing his people for worshipping idols besides God, Mighty and Majestic. So He says: ﴿What are these images to which you are devoted?﴾ that is, to whose worship you are devoted (mu'takifun).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sabbah related to us, Abu Mu'awiyah al-Darir related to us, Sa'd ibn Tarif related to us, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubatah, who said: Ali passed by a people playing chess, and said: "What are these images to which you are devoted?" For one of you to hold a live coal until it goes out is better for him than to touch them.

﴿They said, "We found our fathers worshipping them."﴾ They had no proof other than the practice of their misguided forefathers. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed you were, you and your fathers, in manifest error.﴾ That is: speaking to your fathers, whose practice you took as proof, is like speaking to you; you and they are in error, not on the straight path.

When he belittled their judgment, declared their forefathers misguided, and demeaned their gods, ﴿they said, "Have you brought us the truth, or are you among the jesters?"﴾ They are saying: is this statement coming from you said in jest, or are you sincere in it? For we have never heard of it before you.

﴿He said, "Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them,"﴾ that is: your Lord, besides whom there is no god, is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what they contain of created things, who originated their creation, and who is the Creator of all things. ﴿And I am of those who bear witness to that.﴾ That is: I bear witness that there is no god besides Him and no lord other than Him.

Then the Friend [Abraham] swore an oath, which he made audible to some of his people: "By God, I will surely plot against your idols," meaning he would be eager to harm them and smash them after they had turned their backs and gone off to their festival. They had a festival that they would go out to.

Al-Suddi said: When the time of that festival drew near, his father said, "My son, if you went out with us to our festival, our religion would please you!" So he went out with them. When they were on part of the way, he threw himself down on the ground and said, "I am sick." They kept passing by him while he lay stricken, saying, "What's wrong with you?" and he would say, "I am sick." When most of them had passed and only their weak ones remained, he said: ﴿By God, I will surely plot against your idols﴾, and those remaining heard him.

Abu Ishaq narrated from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abd Allah [Ibn Mas'ud], who said: When Abraham's people went out to their festival, they passed by him and said, "O Abraham, will you not come out with us?" He said, "I am sick." He had said the day before: ﴿By God, I will surely plot against your idols after you have turned your backs and gone away﴾, and some of them heard him.

* *

He did this a third time and was seized, [and he mentioned] the same as the first two times, and he said, 'Pray to God, and I will not harm you.' She prayed, and he was released. She was taken out and given Hajar, and she came back. When Abraham sensed her coming, he turned from his prayer and said, 'Mahyam?' She said, 'God has repelled the plot of the disbelieving, wicked one, and has given me Hajar as a servant.'" Allah the Exalted says, informing about the people of Ibrahim when he said to them what he said: ﴿So they returned to themselves﴾, that is, they blamed themselves for not guarding and protecting their gods. So they said: ﴿Indeed, you are the wrongdoers﴾, that is, in leaving them neglected with no one to watch over them. ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads﴾, that is, they lowered their heads toward the ground, and said: ﴿You have already known that these do not speak﴾. Qatadah said: The people were seized by a terrible confusion, so they said: ﴿You have already known that these do not speak﴾.

As-Suddi said: ﴿Then they were overturned upon their heads﴾, that is, into turmoil (al-fitnah).

Ibn Zayd said: that is, in opinion.

The statement of Qatadah is more apparent in meaning, because they only did that out of bewilderment and helplessness; and for this reason they said to him: ﴿You have already known that these do not speak﴾. How then do you tell us: "Ask them, if they can speak," when you know that they do not speak? At that point, when they had acknowledged this, Ibrahim said to them: ﴿Do you then worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?﴾, that is, if they do not speak, and they neither harm nor benefit, then why do you worship them besides Allah?

﴿Uff to you and to what you worship besides Allah! Do you not then reason?﴾

That is, do you not reflect upon the misguidance and the gross disbelief you are in, which can only be made to pass upon an ignorant, wrongdoing, sinful person? Thus he established the proof against them and obliged them with it. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that was Our argument which We gave Ibrahim against his people﴾ (al-An'am 6:83), to the end of the verse.

But it increased them in faith, and they said, 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 173] [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4563)]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Ibn Hisham narrated to us, Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Asim, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was thrown into the fire, he said: 'O Allah, You are One in the heaven, and I am one on the earth, worshipping You.'" [[Narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, no. (2349) (Kashf al-Astar), and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya (1911), and al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad (10/346) through the route of Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i. Al-Bazzar said: "We do not know of anyone who narrated it from 'Asim except Abu Ja'far, and no one narrated it from him except Ishaq, and we did not hear it except from Abu Hisham." I say: 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs is spoken of (as weak).]]

It is narrated that when they began to bind him, he said: "There is no god but You; glory be to You; to You is the praise, to You is the dominion; You have no partner." [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/642), from Arqam.]]

Shu'ayb al-Jiba'i said: "He was sixteen years old." But Allah knows best.

Some of the early scholars (al-salaf) mentioned that Jibril appeared to him while he was in the air and said: "Do you have a need?" He said: "As for you, no. But as for Allah, yes."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said — and it is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas — that when Ibrahim was thrown, the keeper of the rain began to say: "When am I commanded to send down the rain, so that I may send it?" He said: So the command of Allah came more swiftly than his command. Allah (Mighty and Majestic) said: ﴿O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim.﴾ He said: No fire remained on earth but was extinguished.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: On that day no one benefited from fire, and the fire burned nothing of Ibrahim except his bonds.

Al-Thawri narrated, from al-A'mash, from a shaykh, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib: ﴿We said: O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim.﴾ [He said: It became cool upon him until it nearly killed him, until it was said: ﴿and safety﴾.] He said: It did not harm him.

Ibn 'Abbas and Abu al-'Aliyah said: Had Allah (Mighty and Majestic) not said ﴿and safety﴾, its coldness would have harmed Ibrahim.

Juwaybir narrated from al-Dahhak regarding ﴿be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim﴾: They made for him an enclosure of thick firewood and kindled the fire in it from every side. He awoke and nothing of it had touched him, until Allah extinguished it. He said: And they mention that Jibril was with him, wiping the sweat from his face, and nothing of it touched him except that.

Al-Suddi said: The angel of shade was with him in it.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Yusuf ibn Musa narrated to us, Mihran narrated to us, Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, who said: I was informed that when Ibrahim was thrown into the fire, he (Ibrahim) remained in it, either forty or fifty (days). He said: I was never, in days and nights, better in life than when I was in it. I wished that my whole life and living were like my living when I was in it.

Abu Zur'a ibn 'Amr ibn Jarir narrated, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: Indeed the best thing said by Abu Ibrahim (when the enclosure was lifted from him while he was in the fire, and he found him sprinkling his brow) was, at that moment: "How excellent a Lord is your Lord, O Ibrahim!"

Qatadah said: On that day no creature came but it extinguished the fire from him, except the gecko (al-wazagh). Al-Zuhri said: The Prophet (ﷺ) ordered its killing and named it "fuwaysiq" (the mischievous one). [[This comes from the hadith of Umm Sharik: narrated by al-Bukhari, no. (3307), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2237).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu 'Ubayd Allah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to us; my paternal uncle narrated to me; Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, that Nafi' narrated to him, who said: The freedwoman of al-Fakih ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi narrated to me, saying: I entered upon 'A'ishah and saw in her house a spear. I said: "O Mother of the Believers, what do you do with this spear?" She said: "We kill with it these geckos. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'When Ibrahim was thrown into the fire, there was no creature on earth but it was extinguishing the fire, except the gecko, for it was blowing upon Ibrahim.'" So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded us to kill it. [[Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (6/83, 109) and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (3231), through the route of Nafi' from Sa'ibah, freedwoman of al-Fakih.]]

For this reason He said: ﴿And We delivered him from the town that used to commit abominations. Indeed they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient. * And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous﴾.

The Almighty says, informing about Ibrahim (Abraham), that Allah delivered him from the fire of his people and brought him out from among them as an emigrant to the land of Sham (Greater Syria), to the holy land within it, as Ar-Rabi' ibn Anas related from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, concerning His words: ﴿to the land which We have blessed for all the worlds﴾. He said: "It is Sham, and there is no sweet water except that it flows from beneath the rock."

Abu al-'Aliyah also said the same.

Qatadah said: "He was in the land of Iraq, and Allah delivered him to Sham. [It was said of Sham: 'the pillar of the abode of emigration (dar al-hijrah)'. Whatever is lacking from the land is added to Sham, and whatever is lacking from Sham is added to Palestine.] [[Addition from MS. F.]] It was said: 'It is the land of the gathering and the dispersal (al-mahshar wal-manshar), and in it 'Isa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary), peace be upon him, will descend, and in it the false messiah (al-Masih al-Dajjal) will be destroyed.'"

Ka'b al-Ahbar said concerning His words ﴿to the land which We have blessed for all the worlds﴾: "It is Harran."

As-Suddi said: "Ibrahim and Lut set out towards Sham. Ibrahim met Sarah, who was the daughter of the king of Harran, and she had criticised her people regarding their religion, so he married her on condition that he would not change her."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) narrated it, and it is gharib (weak/unusual). [The well-known view is that she was his cousin, and that he went forth with her as an emigrant from his land.] [[Addition from MS. F.]]

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "To Makkah. Do you not hear His words: ﴿Indeed, the first House appointed for mankind is the one at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds﴾ [Al 'Imran: 96]?"

* *

As for His words: ﴿And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as an additional gift (nafilah)﴾, 'Ata' and Mujahid said: "A gift (atiyyah)."

Ibn 'Abbas, Qatadah and al-Hakam ibn 'Uyaynah said: "Nafilah is the son's son (grandson), meaning that Ya'qub (Jacob) was the son of Ishaq (Isaac), as He said: ﴿So We gave her glad tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob﴾ [Hud: 71]."

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "He asked for one (child), saying: ﴿My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous﴾ [As-Saffat: 100], so Allah gave him Isaac and added to him Jacob as an additional gift."

﴿And We made them all righteous﴾, meaning all of them were people of goodness and righteousness. ﴿And We made them leaders﴾, meaning they were followed. ﴿Guiding by Our command﴾, meaning they called to Allah by His permission. For this reason He said: ﴿And We revealed to them the doing of good deeds, the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakah﴾, which is the conjunction of the specific over the general ('atf al-khass 'ala al-'amm). ﴿And they were worshippers of Us﴾, meaning they did what they commanded people to do.

Then He mentioned Lut, who was Lut ibn Haran ibn Azar. He had believed in Ibrahim, followed him, and emigrated with him, as the Most High said: ﴿So Lut believed him, and said: "Indeed I am emigrating to my Lord"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 26]. Allah gave him judgement and knowledge, revealed to him, made him a prophet, and sent him to Sodom and its territories. They opposed and denied him, so Allah destroyed them and overturned them, as He related their story in more than one place in His Mighty Book. For this reason He said: ﴿And We delivered him from the town that used to commit abominations. Indeed they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient. * And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was among the righteous﴾.

Allah, the Exalted, informs about His answering His servant and messenger Nuh (peace be upon him) when he invoked against his people after they denied him: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overcome, so help [me]"﴾ [al-Qamar 54:10], and ﴿Nuh said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except a wicked disbeliever"﴾ [Nuh 71:26-27]. Therefore He says here: ﴿When he called out before, so We answered him and saved him and his family﴾, i.e., those who believed in him, as He said: ﴿Except for your family, excluding those already decreed against and those who have believed. And none believed with him except a few﴾ [Hud 11:40].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿from the great distress﴾, i.e., from the severity, the denial, and the harm, for he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, calling them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and only a few of them believed in him. They would target him with harm and would counsel one another, generation after generation and age after age, to oppose him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We supported him against the people﴾, i.e., We saved him and delivered him, granting him victory over the people ﴿who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all﴾, i.e., Allah destroyed them with a comprehensive destruction, and He left not a single one of them upon the face of the earth, since their prophet had invoked against them.

Allah, the Exalted, informs about His answering His servant and messenger Nuh (peace be upon him) when he invoked against his people after they denied him: ﴿So he called upon his Lord, "I am overcome, so help [me]"﴾ [al-Qamar 54:10], and ﴿Nuh said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except a wicked disbeliever"﴾ [Nuh 71:26-27]. Therefore He says here: ﴿When he called out before, so We answered him and saved him and his family﴾, i.e., those who believed in him, as He said: ﴿Except for your family, excluding those already decreed against and those who have believed. And none believed with him except a few﴾ [Hud 11:40].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿from the great distress﴾, i.e., from the severity, the denial, and the harm, for he remained among them a thousand years minus fifty years, calling them to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and only a few of them believed in him. They would target him with harm and would counsel one another, generation after generation and age after age, to oppose him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We supported him against the people﴾, i.e., We saved him and delivered him, granting him victory over the people ﴿who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all﴾, i.e., Allah destroyed them with a comprehensive destruction, and He left not a single one of them upon the face of the earth, since their prophet had invoked against them.

Ibn Ishaq narrated from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud: "That tilth was a vineyard whose grape clusters had come out." Shurayh also said the same.

Ibn Abbas said: "An-Nafsh (the grazing of the flock at night) means grazing."

Shurayh, az-Zuhri and Qatadah said: "An-nafsh is at night." Qatadah added: "And al-haml is by day."

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb and Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to us, both saying: al-Maharibi narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning His words, ﴿And Dawud and Sulayman, when they judged concerning the tilth, when the sheep of the people grazed in it﴾: "It was a vineyard whose grape clusters had come out, and [the sheep] destroyed it." He said: "Dawud ruled that the sheep should go to the owner of the vineyard. Sulayman said: 'Other than this, O Prophet of Allah!' He said: 'And what is that?' He said: 'You hand the vineyard over to the owner of the sheep, and he tends it until it returns to how it was. And you hand the sheep over to the owner of the vineyard, and he benefits from them, until when the vineyard is as it was, you return the vineyard to its owner and the sheep to its owner.' That is His words, ﴿So We gave understanding of it to Sulayman﴾."

In the same way, al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Ali ibn Zayd, [who said]: Khalifah narrated to us [in f: "Haddathani"], from Ibn Abbas, who said: Dawud [in f, a: "qada"] ruled concerning the sheep for the owners of the tilth. The shepherds went out with the dogs, and Sulayman said to them: "How did he judge between you?" They informed him, and he said: "If I had been in charge of your affair, I would have judged differently than this!" Dawud was informed of that, so he summoned him and said: "How would you judge between them?" He [in f: "Then he said"] said: "I would hand the sheep over to the owner of the tilth, so that he would have its offspring, its milk, its wool and its benefits, and the owners of the sheep would sow for the people of the tilth the same as their tilth. When the tilth reaches the state it was in, the owners of the tilth take back the tilth and return the sheep to their owners."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Khudayj narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Masruq, who said: "The tilth into which the sheep grazed was only a vineyard into which the sheep grazed, and they left no leaf nor a cluster of grapes in it without eating it. So they came to Dawud, and he gave them the sheep [in f: "so the sheep were given"]. Sulayman said: 'No, rather the sheep should be taken, and given [in f: "so it is given"] to the people of the vineyard, so that they have its milk and its benefit, and the people of the sheep are given the vineyard, so they repair it and restore it [in f: "so he restores it and repairs it"], until it returns like what it was on the night the sheep grazed in it. Then the people of the sheep are given their sheep, and the people of the vineyard their vineyard.'"

Shurayh, Murrah, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and others said the same.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Isma'il informed us, from Amir, who said: Two men came to Shurayh. One of them said: "This man's sheep cut up some yarn of mine." Shurayh said: "By day or by night? If it was by day, then the owner of the sheep is free of liability; if it was by night, he is liable." Then he recited: ﴿And Dawud and Sulayman, when they judged concerning the tilth, when [the sheep] grazed in it﴾, to the end of the verse.

What Shurayh said resembles what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from az-Zuhri, from Haram ibn Muhayyisah: that the she-camel of al-Bara' ibn Azib entered an orchard and caused damage in it, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the people of the orchards must guard them by day, and that what the livestock damages by night is the liability of their owners. [Footnote: Al-Musnad (5/435); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3570); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2332). Note: this chain is only the chain of Ibn Majah; as for Ahmad, he narrated it from Malik, Sufyan and Ma'mar from az-Zuhri, and as for Abu Dawud, he narrated it from Ma'mar and al-Awza'i from az-Zuhri.] This hadith has been criticized as defective, and we have expounded on the discussion of it in our book "al-Ahkam". And with Allah is success.

* *

And His words: ﴿So We gave understanding of it to Sulayman, and to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said:
My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Humayd, that when Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah was appointed as a qadi (judge; one who holds judicial office), al-Hasan came to him and wept. He [Iyas] said: "What makes you weep?" He [al-Hasan] said: "O Abu Sa'id, it has reached me that the judges are: a man who strives (ijtihad, exertion of independent judgment) and errs, he is in the Fire; a man whose desire inclined him, he is in the Fire; and a man who strives and is correct, he is in Paradise." Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Indeed, in what Allah has related of the story of Dawud and Sulayman, peace be upon them, and the prophets, there is a ruling which turns back the saying of these people from their statement. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Dawud and Sulayman, when they judged concerning the tilth, when the sheep of the people grazed in it. And We were witness to their judgment.﴾ So Allah praised Sulayman and did not blame Dawud." Then he said (meaning al-Hasan): "Indeed Allah has taken a covenant from the wise men of three things: they do not sell His signs for a small price, they do not follow desire in it, and they do not fear anyone in it." Then he recited: ﴿O Dawud, indeed We have made you a successor upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow desire, lest it mislead you from the way of Allah﴾ [Sad 38:26], and He said: ﴿So do not fear the people, but fear Me﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:44], and He said: ﴿And do not exchange My verses for a small price﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:44].

I say: As for the prophets, peace be upon them, they are all protected from error and supported by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. This is something on which there is no difference among the knowledgeable verifiers of the earlier and later generations. As for others than them, it has been established in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, from Amr ibn al-As, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the judge strives and is correct, he has two rewards; and when he strives and errs, he has one reward." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (7352)]. So this hadith plainly refutes what Iyas imagined, that when a judge strives and errs he is in the Fire. And Allah knows best.

In the Sunan [collections]: "Judges are of three kinds: one judge is in Paradise, and two judges are in the Fire. A man who knew the truth and judged by it, he is in Paradise; a man who judged among the people in ignorance, he is in the Fire; and a man who knew the truth and judged contrary to it, he is in the Fire." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3573); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (5922); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2315)].

Close to this story mentioned in the Qur'an is what Imam Ahmad narrated in his Musnad, where he said: Ali ibn Hafs narrated to us, Warqa' informed us, from Abu az-Zinad, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "While two women were with their two sons, the wolf came and seized one of the two sons. They brought their dispute to Dawud, and he judged it for the elder. They went out. Then Sulayman called them and said: 'Bring me the knife, I will cut it between them.' The younger said: 'May Allah have mercy on you, he is her son; do not cut him,' so he judged it for the younger." [Al-Musnad (2/322)].

Al-Bukhari and Muslim included it in their two Sahihs, and an-Nasa'i titled it in the Book of Judgments: "(Chapter: The judge may suggest the opposite of the ruling in order to ascertain the truth)." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6769); Sahih Muslim no. (1720); Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (5958). The chapter in it is about "the latitude given to the judge to say to a thing he does not do: do it, so that the truth becomes clear to him."]

Similarly is the story narrated by the Hafiz Abu al-Qasim ibn Asakir in the biography of "Sulayman, peace be upon him," in his History, by way of al-Hasan ibn Sufyan, from Safwan ibn Salih, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Bishr, from Qatadah, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas, who mentioned a lengthy story whose summary is: that a beautiful woman in the time of the Children of Israel was solicited by four of their leaders, but she refused each of them. They agreed among themselves against her, and they testified against her before Dawud, peace be upon him, that she had given herself to a dog of hers which she had trained to do that. So he ordered her stoning. When it was the evening of that day, Sulayman sat, and boys like him gathered with him. He took his place as a judge, and four of them dressed in the clothing of those men, and another in the clothing of the woman, and they testified against her that she had given herself to a dog. Sulayman said: "Separate them." He said to the first of them: "What was the color of the dog?" He said: "Black." So he dismissed him, and summoned the other and asked him about its color. He said: "Red." The other said: "Grayish." And the other said: "White." So he ordered them to be killed. That was reported to Dawud, so he summoned those four immediately, and asked them separately about the color of that dog, and they disagreed about it. So he ordered their execution. [Tarikh Dimashq (7/565, manuscript)].

* *

And His words: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] with Dawud, and the birds; and We were doing [that].﴾ This was because of the beauty of his voice in reciting His Book, the Zabur (Psalms). When he chanted it, the birds would stop in the air and respond to him, and the mountains would echo back to him in refrains. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ passed by Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who was reciting the Qur'an at night, and he had a very beautiful voice, he stopped and listened to his recitation, and said: "Indeed he has been given [a voice like] the mizmar (flute) of the family of Dawud." Abu Musa said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I had known you were listening, I would have beautified it for you with the utmost beautification." [The hadith has been mentioned earlier, in the section on the virtues of the Qur'an.]

Abu Uthman an-Nahdi said: "I have never heard a sound of sanj (cymbals), nor barbat (lute), nor mizmar (flute) like the voice of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him. And yet he said: 'He has been given a mizmar from the mazamir (flutes) of the family of Dawud.'"

* *

And His words: ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of armor for you, to protect you from your violence﴾, meaning the making of coats of mail (dur-u': the plural of dir', body armor). Qatadah said: "Before him, coats of armor were only plates; he was the first to link them as rings (mail)." As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We made iron pliable for him: [saying], "Make full coats of mail and calculate the links [properly]"﴾ [Saba' 34:10-11], meaning: do not make the ring too wide so that the pin slips out, and do not make the pin too thick so that the ring breaks. For this reason He said: ﴿to protect you from your violence﴾, meaning: in fighting. ﴿So will you be grateful?﴾, meaning: [grateful for] the favors of Allah upon you, for what He inspired His servant Dawud with, so He taught him this for your sake.

* *

And His words: ﴿And for Sulayman [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully﴾, meaning: We subjected to Sulayman the strong wind, ﴿running at his command toward the land which We had blessed﴾, meaning the land of ash-Sham (Syria), ﴿And We were, of all things, Knowing﴾. This is because he had a carpet of wood on which would be placed everything he needed of the affairs of the kingdom: horses, camels, tents and soldiers. Then he would command the wind to carry it, and it would enter under it, then carry it and lift it up and travel with it, while the birds shaded it from the heat, to wherever he willed on the earth, and then it would land, and his equipment and entourage would be set down. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We subjected to him the wind, running gently at his command wherever he intended﴾ [Sad 38:36], and He said: ﴿Its morning [journey] was a month, and its evening [journey] was a month﴾ [Saba' 34:12].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Abu Sinan, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "There were placed for Sulayman six hundred thousand chairs, and there would sit next to him the believing men of mankind, then behind them would sit the believing jinn, then he would command the birds, and they would shade them, then he would command the wind, and it would carry him (ﷺ) [in a: 'and it would carry them upon him, peace be upon him']."

Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Sulayman would command the wind, and it would gather like a great mountain, like a mountain. Then he would order his carpet to be placed on the highest part of it, and then he would call for a horse of those with wings, and it would rise until it ascended onto his carpet. Then he would command the wind, and it would carry him up to every height short of the sky, while he kept his head bowed, not looking right or left, out of glorification of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and gratitude for what he knew of the smallness of what he was in within the dominion of Allah the Exalted, until the wind sets him down wherever he wishes to set him down.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And of the devils were those who dived for him﴾, meaning: in the water, extracting pearls [and other things]. ﴿And they did other work besides that﴾, meaning: other than that, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound together in chains﴾ [Sad: 37-38].

* *

Rather, he (Sulayman) had authority over them: if he wished he would release them, and if he wished he would imprison whomever he wished of them. For this reason He said: ﴿and others bound together in chains﴾.

* *

And His words: ﴿And for Sulayman [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully﴾, meaning: We subjected to Sulayman the strong wind, ﴿running at his command toward the land which We had blessed﴾, meaning the land of ash-Sham (Syria), ﴿And We were, of all things, Knowing﴾. This is because he had a carpet of wood on which would be placed everything he needed of the affairs of the kingdom: horses, camels, tents and soldiers. Then he would command the wind to carry it, and it would enter under it, then carry it and lift it up and travel with it, while the birds shaded it from the heat, to wherever he willed on the earth, and then it would land, and his equipment and entourage would be set down. Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was mentioned from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Abu Sinan, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "There were placed for Sulayman six hundred thousand chairs, and there would sit next to him the believing men of mankind, then behind them would sit the believing jinn, then he would command the birds, and they would shade them, then he would command the wind, and it would carry him (ﷺ) [in a: 'and it would carry them upon him, peace be upon him']."

Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr said: Sulayman would command the wind, and it would gather like a great mountain, like a mountain. Then he would order his carpet to be placed on the highest part of it, and then he would call for a horse of those with wings, and it would rise until it ascended onto his carpet. Then he would command the wind, and it would carry him up to every height short of the sky, while he kept his head bowed, not looking right or left, out of glorification of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and gratitude for what he knew of the smallness of what he was in within the dominion of Allah the Exalted, until the wind sets him down wherever he wishes to set him down.

And His saying: ﴿And of the devils were those who dived for him﴾, meaning: in the water, extracting pearls [and other things]. ﴿And they did other work besides that﴾, meaning: other than that, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver, and others bound together in chains﴾ [Sad: 37-38].

And His saying: ﴿And We were its guardians﴾ [the text in one manuscript reads "for him"], meaning: Allah guarded him against any of the devils harming him, rather all of them were in His grip and under His subjugation, none of them dared to approach him or draw near to him. Rather, he (Sulayman) had authority over them: if he wished he would release them, and if he wished he would imprison whomever he wished of them. For this reason He said: ﴿and others bound together in chains﴾.

Ibn Ishaq narrated from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud: "That tilth was a vineyard whose grape clusters had come out." Shurayh also said the same.

Ibn Abbas said: "An-Nafsh (the grazing of the flock at night) means grazing."

Shurayh, az-Zuhri and Qatadah said: "An-nafsh is at night." Qatadah added: "And al-haml is by day."

Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb and Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to us, both saying: al-Maharibi narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, concerning His words, ﴿And Dawud and Sulayman, when they judged concerning the tilth, when the sheep of the people grazed in it﴾: "It was a vineyard whose grape clusters had come out, and [the sheep] destroyed it." He said: "Dawud ruled that the sheep should go to the owner of the vineyard. Sulayman said: 'Other than this, O Prophet of Allah!' He said: 'And what is that?' He said: 'You hand the vineyard over to the owner of the sheep, and he tends it until it returns to how it was. And you hand the sheep over to the owner of the vineyard, and he benefits from them, until when the vineyard is as it was, you return the vineyard to its owner and the sheep to its owner.' That is His words, ﴿So We gave understanding of it to Sulayman﴾."

In the same way, al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Ali ibn Zayd, [who said]: Khalifah narrated to us [in f: "Haddathani"], from Ibn Abbas, who said: Dawud [in f, a: "qada"] ruled concerning the sheep for the owners of the tilth. The shepherds went out with the dogs, and Sulayman said to them: "How did he judge between you?" They informed him, and he said: "If I had been in charge of your affair, I would have judged differently than this!" Dawud was informed of that, so he summoned him and said: "How would you judge between them?" He [in f: "Then he said"] said: "I would hand the sheep over to the owner of the tilth, so that he would have its offspring, its milk, its wool and its benefits, and the owners of the sheep would sow for the people of the tilth the same as their tilth. When the tilth reaches the state it was in, the owners of the tilth take back the tilth and return the sheep to their owners."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Khudayj narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Murrah, from Masruq, who said: "The tilth into which the sheep grazed was only a vineyard into which the sheep grazed, and they left no leaf nor a cluster of grapes in it without eating it. So they came to Dawud, and he gave them the sheep [in f: "so the sheep were given"]. Sulayman said: 'No, rather the sheep should be taken, and given [in f: "so it is given"] to the people of the vineyard, so that they have its milk and its benefit, and the people of the sheep are given the vineyard, so they repair it and restore it [in f: "so he restores it and repairs it"], until it returns like what it was on the night the sheep grazed in it. Then the people of the sheep are given their sheep, and the people of the vineyard their vineyard.'"

Shurayh, Murrah, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and others said the same.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Isma'il informed us, from Amir, who said: Two men came to Shurayh. One of them said: "This man's sheep cut up some yarn of mine." Shurayh said: "By day or by night? If it was by day, then the owner of the sheep is free of liability; if it was by night, he is liable." Then he recited: ﴿And Dawud and Sulayman, when they judged concerning the tilth, when [the sheep] grazed in it﴾, to the end of the verse.

What Shurayh said resembles what Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from az-Zuhri, from Haram ibn Muhayyisah: that the she-camel of al-Bara' ibn Azib entered an orchard and caused damage in it, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ruled that the people of the orchards must guard them by day, and that what the livestock damages by night is the liability of their owners. [Footnote: Al-Musnad (5/435); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3570); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2332). Note: this chain is only the chain of Ibn Majah; as for Ahmad, he narrated it from Malik, Sufyan and Ma'mar from az-Zuhri, and as for Abu Dawud, he narrated it from Ma'mar and al-Awza'i from az-Zuhri.] This hadith has been criticized as defective, and we have expounded on the discussion of it in our book "al-Ahkam". And with Allah is success.
