Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says, concerning Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, the trial that befell him in his wealth, his children and his body. He had a great deal of livestock, beasts of burden and crops, many children, and fine dwellings. He was tested in all of that, and it all vanished entirely. Then he was tested in his body. It is said that he was afflicted with leprosy (al-judham) over his whole body, and nothing of him remained sound except his heart and his tongue, with which he remembered Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He was so repulsive that his companions shunned him, and he was isolated in a corner of the town. No one among the people remained who showed him compassion except his wife, who attended to his affairs. It is said that she was in need, so she began serving people for his sake.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The people most severely tested are the prophets, then the righteous, then those most like them, then those most like them." (Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/172), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (2398) and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan no. (4023), from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith.") In another hadith: "A person is tested according to the measure of his religion; if his religion is firm, his trial is increased." (This is part of the preceding hadith, and Allah knows best.)

The Prophet of Allah, Ayyub, peace be upon him, was the ultimate example of patience, and he is cited as the example in this regard.

Yazid ibn Maysarah said: When Allah tested Ayyub, peace be upon him, with the loss of his family, wealth and children, and nothing remained, he praised Allah and said: "I praise You, Lord of lords, who has been good to me. You gave me wealth and children, and no portion of my heart remained that was not filled with them. You took all of that from me and emptied my heart, so nothing stands between me and You. If my enemy Iblis knew what I have done, he would envy me." He said: So Iblis encountered something abhorrent from that.

He said: Ayyub, peace be upon him, also said: "O Lord, You gave me wealth and children, yet no one ever stood at my door complaining of an injustice I had done, and You know this. My bed used to be spread for me, and I would leave it, saying to myself: 'O self, you were not created for soft beds. I only abandoned it seeking Your face.'" Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

A lengthy account is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih, transmitted by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim with its chain, and other later exegetes have mentioned it. It contains strange elements, and we have left it out for the sake of brevity. (Tafsir al-Tabari (1/42).)

It is narrated that he remained in affliction for a long period. Then they differed about what prompted him to make this supplication. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Ayyub, peace be upon him, was tested for seven years and some months, lying on the refuse heap of the Children of Israel, with worms moving over his body. Then Allah relieved him, magnified his reward, and praised him well.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: He remained in affliction for three years, neither more nor less.

al-Suddi said: Ayyub's flesh fell away until only the sinews and bones remained. His wife would attend to him and bring him food she had earned. When his suffering lengthened, his wife said to him: "O Ayyub, if you were to call upon your Lord, He might relieve you." He said: "I lived seventy years in health; is it so much for me to be patient with Him for seventy years?" She became distressed at this and went away. She would work for people for wages and bring him what she earned, and feed him. Iblis went to two men from Palestine who were his friends and brothers. He came to them and said: "Your brother Ayyub has been struck with such-and-such affliction. Go to him, visit him, and bring with you wine from your land, for if he drinks from it he will be cured." So they came to him, and when they looked at him they wept. He said: "Who are you?" They said: "We are so-and-so and so-and-so!" He welcomed them and said: "Welcome to those who do not shun me in time of trial." They said: "O Ayyub, perhaps you concealed something and displayed something else, and that is why Allah has tested you?" He raised his head toward the sky and said: "He knows. I have concealed nothing that I displayed otherwise. But my Lord has tested me so that He may see whether I will be patient or become distressed." They said to him: "O Ayyub, drink from our wine, for if you drink from it you will be cured." He became angry and said: "The wicked one came to you and commanded you with this? Your speech, your food and your drink are forbidden to me." So they rose from his presence. His wife went out to work for people, and she baked for a household that had a child; they gave her a loaf, and the boy was sleeping, and they disliked waking him, so they gave it to her.

She brought it to Ayyub, and he disowned it and said: "You never used to bring me this before; what has happened to you today?" She told him the story. He said: "Perhaps the boy has awoken, looked for the loaf, not found it, and is now crying for his family. Go back to him with it." She set off until she reached the people's courtyard, and one of their goats butted her, and she said: "May Ayyub the sinner be ruined!" When she climbed up, she found the boy had awoken, was seeking the loaf, and was crying for his family, accepting nothing from them but it. She said: "May Allah have mercy on Ayyub," and she handed him the loaf and returned. Then Iblis came to her in the form of a physician and said: "Your husband's sickness has lasted long. If he wishes to be cured, let him take a fly, slaughter it in the name of the idol of such-and-such people, and he will be cured and will repent afterward." She told Ayyub this, and he said: "The wicked one has come to you. By Allah, if I am cured, I will flog you one hundred lashes." She went out seeking provision for him, but her livelihood was withheld, and no household she came to would employ her. When this became hard for her and she feared for Ayyub from hunger, she cut off a lock of her hair and sold it to a girl from the daughters of the nobles, and they gave her a large quantity of good food. She brought it to Ayyub, and when he saw it he disowned it and said: "From where do you have this?" She said: "I worked for people and they fed me." He ate from it. The next day she went out seeking work but found none, so she again cut off a lock of her hair and sold it to that girl, and they gave her some of that food. She brought it to Ayyub, and he said: "By Allah, I will not eat it until I know where it comes from." So she removed her headscarf, and when he saw her head shaved he grieved intensely. At that point he called upon his Lord, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Abu Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from Nawf al-Bikali: that the devil who struck Ayyub was called "Sawt" [in some copies: "Mabsut"]. He said: Ayyub's wife would say: "Call upon Allah so that He may heal you," but he would not supplicate, until a group of the Children of Israel passed by him, and some of them said to others: "He has only suffered what he has suffered because of a great sin he committed." At that point he said: "My Lord, indeed adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful."

And my father narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Ayyub, peace be upon him, had two brothers who came one day, but could not approach him because of his smell, so they stood at a distance. One of them said to the other: "If Allah had known any good in Ayyub, He would not have tested him with this." Ayyub grieved at their words with a grief he had never felt over anything, and said: "O Allah, if You know that I never spent a night full while knowing of a hungry person, then vindicate me." He was vindicated from the sky while they both heard. Then he said: "O Allah, if You know that I never had two shirts, while knowing of a naked person, then vindicate me." He was vindicated from the sky while they both heard. He said: "O Allah, by Your might," then fell prostrate, then said: "O Allah, by Your might, I will never raise my head until You relieve me." He did not raise his head until it was removed from him.

Ibn Abi Hatim also related it from another route, traced to the Prophet ﷺ, with similar wording. He said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la informed us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Uqayl, from al-Zuhri, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The affliction of the Prophet of Allah Ayyub lasted eighteen years. He was abandoned by near and far, except for two men among his brothers, who were among his closest brothers. They would visit him morning and evening. One of them said to his companion: 'Know, by Allah, that Ayyub has committed a sin no one among the worlds has committed.' His companion said: 'What is that?' He said: 'For eighteen years Allah has not shown him mercy to remove what afflicts him.' When they came to him, the man could not refrain from mentioning this to him. Ayyub, peace be upon him, said: 'I do not know what you are saying, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows that I used to pass by two men quarreling and remembering Allah, so I would return to my house and make expiation for them, out of dislike that they should mention Allah except in what is right.'" He said: He used to go out for his needs, and when he finished them his wife would hold his hand until he reached home. One day she was late to him, and it was revealed to Ayyub where he stood: "Strike with your foot; this is a cool bath and a drink." (Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih no. (2091) "Mawarid", by way of Harmalah ibn Yahya from Ibn Wahb with similar wording.)

The raising of this hadith to the Prophet is very strange.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, Ali ibn Zayd informed us, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Allah clothed him in a garment from Paradise. Ayyub withdrew and sat in a corner, and his wife came but did not recognize him. She said: "O servant of Allah, where has the afflicted man who was here gone? Perhaps the dogs or the wolves took him." She kept speaking with him for a while. He said: "Woe to you! I am Ayyub!" She said: "Are you mocking me, servant of Allah?" He said: "Woe to you! I am Ayyub; Allah has restored my body to me."

Ibn Abbas also said: He was given back his wealth and children before his eyes, and with them their like.

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Allah revealed to Ayyub: "I have restored to you your family and your wealth, and their like along with them. Bathe in this water, for in it is your cure. [And he said] also: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Amr ibn Marzuq narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Nadr ibn Anas, from Bashir ibn Nahik, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "When Allah restored Ayyub to health, He rained upon him locusts of gold, and he began to take them in his hand and place them in his garment." He said: "It was said to him: 'O Ayyub, are you not satisfied?' He said: 'O Lord, who could be satisfied with Your mercy?'"

Its origin is in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) [al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/582) by several routes from Amr ibn Marzuq; the origin of the hadith will come in Sahih al-Bukhari at the commentary on verse 42 of Surah Sad], and it will come up again in another place.

And his saying: ﴿And We gave him his family and the like of them with them﴾. It has already been reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "They were returned to him in their own persons." Al-'Awfi also reported the same from Ibn 'Abbas. The like of this was reported from Ibn Mas'ud and Mujahid, and al-Hasan and Qatadah also said so.

Some have claimed that the name of his wife was Rahmah. If he took this from the context of the verse, then he has gone far from the intended meaning. If he took it from the reports of the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab, Jews and Christians), and it is authentically transmitted from them, then it is among those things that are neither to be believed nor to be denied. Ibn 'Asakir (may God have mercy on him) named her in his History. He said: "It is said her name was Layya, daughter of Mansha ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qub ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim." He said: "It is also said: Layya, daughter of Ya'qub (peace be upon him), the wife of Ayyub, was with him in the land of al-Bathaniyyah."

Mujahid said: It was said to him: "O Ayyub, your family is awaiting you in Paradise. If you wish, We will bring them to you, or if you wish, We will leave them for you in Paradise and give you the like of them." He said: "No, rather leave them for me in Paradise." So they were left for him in Paradise, and the like of them was given to him in this world.

Hammad ibn Zayd reported from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from Nawf al-Bikali, who said: "His reward for them was given in the Hereafter, and the like of them was given to him in this world." He said: "I related this to Mutarrif, and he said: 'I did not know its meaning before today.'"

The like of this has been reported from Qatadah, al-Suddi, and many others of the early generations (al-salaf, the pious predecessors). And God knows best.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says, concerning Ayyub (Job), peace be upon him, the trial that befell him in his wealth, his children and his body. He had a great deal of livestock, beasts of burden and crops, many children, and fine dwellings. He was tested in all of that, and it all vanished entirely. Then he was tested in his body. It is said that he was afflicted with leprosy (al-judham) over his whole body, and nothing of him remained sound except his heart and his tongue, with which he remembered Allah, Mighty and Majestic. He was so repulsive that his companions shunned him, and he was isolated in a corner of the town. No one among the people remained who showed him compassion except his wife, who attended to his affairs. It is said that she was in need, so she began serving people for his sake.

The Prophet ﷺ said: "The people most severely tested are the prophets, then the righteous, then those most like them, then those most like them." (Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (1/172), al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan no. (2398) and Ibn Majah in al-Sunan no. (4023), from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah be pleased with him. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith.") In another hadith: "A person is tested according to the measure of his religion; if his religion is firm, his trial is increased." (This is part of the preceding hadith, and Allah knows best.)

The Prophet of Allah, Ayyub, peace be upon him, was the ultimate example of patience, and he is cited as the example in this regard.

Yazid ibn Maysarah said: When Allah tested Ayyub, peace be upon him, with the loss of his family, wealth and children, and nothing remained, he praised Allah and said: "I praise You, Lord of lords, who has been good to me. You gave me wealth and children, and no portion of my heart remained that was not filled with them. You took all of that from me and emptied my heart, so nothing stands between me and You. If my enemy Iblis knew what I have done, he would envy me." He said: So Iblis encountered something abhorrent from that.

He said: Ayyub, peace be upon him, also said: "O Lord, You gave me wealth and children, yet no one ever stood at my door complaining of an injustice I had done, and You know this. My bed used to be spread for me, and I would leave it, saying to myself: 'O self, you were not created for soft beds. I only abandoned it seeking Your face.'" Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

A lengthy account is related from Wahb ibn Munabbih, transmitted by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim with its chain, and other later exegetes have mentioned it. It contains strange elements, and we have left it out for the sake of brevity. (Tafsir al-Tabari (1/42).)

Then Allah relieved him, magnified his reward, and praised him well.

And his saying: ﴿A mercy from Us﴾, meaning: We did this for him as a mercy from God to him. ﴿And a reminder for the worshippers﴾, meaning: We made him an example in this, so that the people of affliction would not think that We inflicted that upon them only because of their humiliation before Us, and so that they would take him as a model in patience with what God decrees and with His testing of His servants with whatever He wills. And to Him belongs perfect wisdom in that.

Regarding Ismail, what is meant is the son of Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil), upon them both be peace, and his mention has already preceded in Surah Maryam, and likewise Idris, peace be upon him [[See the commentary on verses 54-57.]]. As for Dhul-Kifl, the apparent meaning from the context is that he is not mentioned alongside the prophets except that he was a prophet. Others said: he was only a righteous man, and he was a just king and an equitable judge, and Ibn Jarir hesitated regarding this, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Juraij reported from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿And Dhul-Kifl﴾, he said: "A righteous man, not a prophet, who undertook for the prophet of his people that he would take care of the affairs of his people for him, establish them for him, and judge among them with justice. So he did that, and so he was named Dhul-Kifl." Likewise Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid as well.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: When al-Yasa' grew old, he said: "If only I could appoint a man over the people to govern them during my lifetime, so that I may see how he governs." So he gathered the people and said: "Who will take on from me [the duty] with three conditions: I will appoint him, he fasts by day, stands in prayer by night, and does not become angry." Then a man stood up whom the eye looked down upon, and said: "I will." He said: "You fast by day, stand in prayer by night, and do not become angry?" He said: "Yes." He said: So he dismissed them that day, and said the same on the next day, and the people remained silent, and that man stood up and said: "I will." So he appointed him. He said: Iblis began saying to the devils: "Upon you is so-and-so." But they were unable to [overcome] that man. He said: "Leave me and him." So he came to him in the form of a feeble, elderly shaykh, and came to him when he had lain down for the midday rest (al-qa'ilah), and he used not to sleep by night or by day except for that nap. So he knocked on the door, and he said: "Who is this?" He said: "An elderly, wronged shaykh." He said: So he got up and opened the door, and the shaykh began to recount to him, saying: "Between me and my people there is a dispute, and they have wronged me, and they have done this and that to me." He kept prolonging it until the time of the afternoon came and the midday rest had passed. He said: "When I go out, come to me and I will take your right for you." So he left and went out. He sat in his assembly, and began looking to see whether he could see the shaykh, but he did not see him, so he got up to go after him. When the next day came, he began judging between the people while waiting for him, but did not see him. When he returned to the midday rest and lay down, he came to him, knocked on the door, and he said: "Who is this?" The elderly, wronged shaykh said: "..." So he opened the door for him and said: "Did I not tell you: when I sit, come to me?" He said: "They are the most wicked people; when they know that you are seated, they say: 'We will give you your right,' and when you rise they deny me." He said: "Go, and when I go out, come to me." He said: So the midday rest escaped him, he went out and began waiting for him while not seeing him, and drowsiness overcame him, so he said to some of his family: "Do not let anyone approach this door until I sleep, for sleep has overcome me." When that hour came, he came to him, and the man said to him: "Behind you, behind you!" He said: "I came to him yesterday, and mentioned my matter to him, and he said: 'No, by Allah, he has commanded us not to let anyone approach him.'" When he was overpowered, he looked and saw a window in the house, so he climbed through it, and behold, he was in the house, and behold, he was knocking on the door from inside. He said: The man awoke and said: "O so-and-so, did I not command you?" He said: "As for from my side, by Allah, I was not reached, so look from where you were reached." He said: So he went to the door, and behold, it was locked as he had locked it, and behold, the man was with him in the house, so he recognized him and said: "O enemy of Allah?" He said: "Yes, you have defeated me in everything, so I did what you see to anger you." So Allah named him Dhul-Kifl, because he undertook a matter and fulfilled it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/59).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim similarly reported it, from the narration of Zuhayr ibn Ishaq, from Dawud, from Mujahid, with its like.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: There was a judge among the Children of Israel, and death came upon him, and he said: "Who will take my place on condition that he does not become angry?" He said: A man said: "I will." So he was named Dhul-Kifl. He said: He would pray the whole night, then in the morning he would fast and judge between the people. He said: And he had an hour of midday rest. He said: So it was like that, until Satan came to him during his sleep. His companions said to him: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "A poor person has a right against a man, and he has overpowered me regarding it." They said: "Stay as you are until he wakes up." He said: He was lying above (him) asleep. He said: So he began shouting deliberately until he woke him, he said: He heard, and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "A poor person has a right against a man." He said: "Go and tell him: let him give you." He said: "He has refused." He said: "Go yourself to him." He said: So he went, then came the next day, and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "I went to him, and he did not even raise his head to your words." He said: "Go to him and tell him: let him give you your right." He said: So he went, then came the next day at the time he had said. He said: His companions said to him: "Get out, may Allah do to you [what He will], you come every day when he sleeps; will you not leave him to sleep?" So he began shouting: "Because I am a poor person, if I were rich?" He said: He heard again and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "I went to him and he struck me." He said: "Walk, until I come with you." He said: So he was holding his hand, and when he saw him he went with him, and he shook his hand off him and fled.

Likewise it has been narrated from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, Muhammad ibn Qays, Ibn Hujayrah al-Akbar, and others among the early scholars, something close to this story, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Jamahir narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Bashir informed us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Abu Kinanah ibn al-Akhnas, who said: I heard al-Ash'ari saying upon this pulpit: "Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but there was among the Children of Israel (he meant) a righteous man who would pray one hundred prayers every day, and Dhul-Kifl undertook for him after him, and he would pray one hundred prayers every day, so he was named Dhul-Kifl."

Ibn Jarir has narrated it from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah who said: "Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said..." and he mentioned it as disconnected (munqati') [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/60).]], and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad narrated a strange (gharib) hadith, saying:

Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Sa'd, the freedman of Talhah, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a hadith which, had I heard it only once or twice—until he counted seven times—but I have heard it more than that, he said: "Al-Kifl was from the Children of Israel, who did not refrain from any sin he committed. A woman came to him and he gave her sixty dinars on condition that he would have intercourse with her. When he sat with her in the position of a man with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said: 'What makes you weep? Did I force you?' She said: 'No, but this is a deed I have never done before, and only need compelled me to it.' He said: 'You do this and you have never done it before?' Then he got down and said: 'Go, the dinars are yours.' Then he said: 'By Allah, Al-Kifl will never disobey Allah again.' He died that night, and in the morning it was written on his door: 'Allah has forgiven Al-Kifl.'" [[Musnad (2/23).]]

Thus in this narration the word is "al-Kifl" without an addition, and Allah knows best. This hadith has not been recorded by anyone from the authors of the Six Books [[I say: rather, al-Tirmidhi recorded it in his Sunan under no. (2496) through the route of 'Ubayd ibn Asbat from his father with it, and said: "This is a hasan hadith; Shayban and more than one have narrated it from al-A'mash like this, raising it (to the Prophet), and some have narrated from al-A'mash without raising it."]], and its chain is strange (gharib). In any case, if the wording is "al-Kifl" and not "Dhul-Kifl," then perhaps it refers to another man, and Allah knows best.

Regarding Ismail, what is meant is the son of Ibrahim the Friend (al-Khalil), upon them both be peace, and his mention has already preceded in Surah Maryam, and likewise Idris, peace be upon him [[See the commentary on verses 54-57.]]. As for Dhul-Kifl, the apparent meaning from the context is that he is not mentioned alongside the prophets except that he was a prophet. Others said: he was only a righteous man, and he was a just king and an equitable judge, and Ibn Jarir hesitated regarding this, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Juraij reported from Mujahid, regarding his saying: ﴿And Dhul-Kifl﴾, he said: "A righteous man, not a prophet, who undertook for the prophet of his people that he would take care of the affairs of his people for him, establish them for him, and judge among them with justice. So he did that, and so he was named Dhul-Kifl." Likewise Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid as well.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: When al-Yasa' grew old, he said: "If only I could appoint a man over the people to govern them during my lifetime, so that I may see how he governs." So he gathered the people and said: "Who will take on from me [the duty] with three conditions: I will appoint him, he fasts by day, stands in prayer by night, and does not become angry." Then a man stood up whom the eye looked down upon, and said: "I will." He said: "You fast by day, stand in prayer by night, and do not become angry?" He said: "Yes." He said: So he dismissed them that day, and said the same on the next day, and the people remained silent, and that man stood up and said: "I will." So he appointed him. He said: Iblis began saying to the devils: "Upon you is so-and-so." But they were unable to [overcome] that man. He said: "Leave me and him." So he came to him in the form of a feeble, elderly shaykh, and came to him when he had lain down for the midday rest (al-qa'ilah), and he used not to sleep by night or by day except for that nap. So he knocked on the door, and he said: "Who is this?" He said: "An elderly, wronged shaykh." He said: So he got up and opened the door, and the shaykh began to recount to him, saying: "Between me and my people there is a dispute, and they have wronged me, and they have done this and that to me." He kept prolonging it until the time of the afternoon came and the midday rest had passed. He said: "When I go out, come to me and I will take your right for you." So he left and went out. He sat in his assembly, and began looking to see whether he could see the shaykh, but he did not see him, so he got up to go after him. When the next day came, he began judging between the people while waiting for him, but did not see him. When he returned to the midday rest and lay down, he came to him, knocked on the door, and he said: "Who is this?" The elderly, wronged shaykh said: "..." So he opened the door for him and said: "Did I not tell you: when I sit, come to me?" He said: "They are the most wicked people; when they know that you are seated, they say: 'We will give you your right,' and when you rise they deny me." He said: "Go, and when I go out, come to me." He said: So the midday rest escaped him, he went out and began waiting for him while not seeing him, and drowsiness overcame him, so he said to some of his family: "Do not let anyone approach this door until I sleep, for sleep has overcome me." When that hour came, he came to him, and the man said to him: "Behind you, behind you!" He said: "I came to him yesterday, and mentioned my matter to him, and he said: 'No, by Allah, he has commanded us not to let anyone approach him.'" When he was overpowered, he looked and saw a window in the house, so he climbed through it, and behold, he was in the house, and behold, he was knocking on the door from inside. He said: The man awoke and said: "O so-and-so, did I not command you?" He said: "As for from my side, by Allah, I was not reached, so look from where you were reached." He said: So he went to the door, and behold, it was locked as he had locked it, and behold, the man was with him in the house, so he recognized him and said: "O enemy of Allah?" He said: "Yes, you have defeated me in everything, so I did what you see to anger you." So Allah named him Dhul-Kifl, because he undertook a matter and fulfilled it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/59).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim similarly reported it, from the narration of Zuhayr ibn Ishaq, from Dawud, from Mujahid, with its like.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: There was a judge among the Children of Israel, and death came upon him, and he said: "Who will take my place on condition that he does not become angry?" He said: A man said: "I will." So he was named Dhul-Kifl. He said: He would pray the whole night, then in the morning he would fast and judge between the people. He said: So he began shouting deliberately until he woke him, he said: He heard, and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "A poor person has a right against a man." He said: "Go and tell him: let him give you." He said: "He has refused." He said: "Go yourself to him." He said: So he went, then came the next day, and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "I went to him, and he did not even raise his head to your words." He said: "Go to him and tell him: let him give you your right." He said: So he went, then came the next day at the time he had said. So he began shouting: "Because I am a poor person, if I were rich?" He said: He heard again and said: "What is wrong with you?" He said: "I went to him and he struck me." Likewise it has been narrated from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, Muhammad ibn Qays, Ibn Hujayrah al-Akbar, and others among the early scholars, something close to this story, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Jamahir narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Bashir informed us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Abu Kinanah ibn al-Akhnas, who said: I heard al-Ash'ari saying upon this pulpit: "Dhul-Kifl was not a prophet, but there was among the Children of Israel (he meant) a righteous man who would pray one hundred prayers every day, and Dhul-Kifl undertook for him after him, and he would pray one hundred prayers every day, so he was named Dhul-Kifl."

Ibn Jarir has narrated it from the narration of 'Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah who said: "Abu Musa al-Ash'ari said..." and he mentioned it as disconnected (munqati') [[Tafsir al-Tabari (17/60).]], and Allah knows best.

Imam Ahmad narrated a strange (gharib) hadith, saying:

Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Abdullah, from Sa'd, the freedman of Talhah, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a hadith which, had I heard it only once or twice—until he counted seven times—but I have heard it more than that, he said: "Al-Kifl was from the Children of Israel, who did not refrain from any sin he committed. A woman came to him and he gave her sixty dinars on condition that he would have intercourse with her. When he sat with her in the position of a man with his wife, she trembled and wept. He said: 'What makes you weep? Did I force you?' She said: 'No, but this is a deed I have never done before, and only need compelled me to it.' He said: 'You do this and you have never done it before?' Then he got down and said: 'Go, the dinars are yours.' Then he said: 'By Allah, Al-Kifl will never disobey Allah again.' He died that night, and in the morning it was written on his door: 'Allah has forgiven Al-Kifl.'" [[Musnad (2/23).]]

Thus in this narration the word is "al-Kifl" without an addition, and Allah knows best. This hadith has not been recorded by anyone from the authors of the Six Books [[I say: rather, al-Tirmidhi recorded it in his Sunan under no. (2496) through the route of 'Ubayd ibn Asbat from his father with it, and said: "This is a hasan hadith; Shayban and more than one have narrated it from al-A'mash like this, raising it (to the Prophet), and some have narrated from al-A'mash without raising it."]], and its chain is strange (gharib). In any case, if the wording is "al-Kifl" and not "Dhul-Kifl," then perhaps it refers to another man, and Allah knows best.

This story is mentioned here, in Surat as-Saffat, and in Surat Nun. [[Surat as-Saffat, verses 139-148, and Surat Nun (al-Qalam), verses 48-50.]] The reason is that Allah sent Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, to the people of the town of Nineveh, which is a town in the land of Mosul. He called them to Allah, but they refused him and persisted in their disbelief. So he left them in anger, and he promised them punishment after three days. When they were certain of this, and knew that a prophet does not lie, they went out into the desert with their children, their livestock and their herds, and they separated the mothers from their young. Then they humbled themselves before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and cried out to Him, and the camels bellowed with their young, the cows lowed with their calves, and the sheep bleated with their lambs. So Allah removed the punishment from them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith would benefit it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We let them enjoy for a time.﴾ [Yunus: 98].

As for Yunus, peace be upon him, he went and boarded a ship with some people, and the ship was tossed by the waves, and they feared they would drown. They cast lots over a man from among them to throw overboard, so that they could lighten the ship, and the lot fell upon Yunus. They refused to throw him, then they repeated the lot and it fell upon him again, and they refused. Then they repeated it and it fell upon him again. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾ [As-Saffat: 141], meaning the lot fell upon him. Yunus, peace be upon him, stood up, stripped off his clothes, and threw himself into the sea. Allah, glorified and exalted, had sent from the Green Sea, as Ibn Mas'ud said, a whale that cuts through the seas, and it came and swallowed Yunus when he threw himself from the ship. Allah revealed to that whale that it should not eat his flesh nor break his bones; for Yunus is not provision for you, rather your belly is a prison for him.

* *

His saying: ﴿Dhu'n-Nun﴾ means the whale; the attribution to it is correct on this basis.

* *

His saying: ﴿when he went off in anger﴾: al-Dahhak said, "to his people." ﴿So he thought that We would not decree against him﴾ [meaning: that We would not constrict him in the belly of the whale. This is reported similarly from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it, citing as evidence the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it. Allah will bring about ease after hardship﴾ (At-Talaq: 7).

Ata al-Awfi said: ﴿So he thought that We would not decree against him﴾, meaning, "We would not decree (qadha) against him." It seems he took this to mean "qaddara" (to decree), since the Arabs say qadara and qaddara with the same meaning. A poet said: "Never shall that time that has passed return... Blessed are you; whatever you decree, will be; to you belongs the command..."

From this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then the waters met for a matter already decreed﴾ [Al-Qamar: 12], meaning, it was decreed (quddira).

* *

His saying: ﴿So he called out in the darknesses: "There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers."﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: the darkness of the belly of the whale, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night. Similarly it was reported from Ibn Abbas, Amr ibn Maymun, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan and Qatadah.

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd said: the darkness of a whale within the belly of another whale, in the darkness of the sea.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and others said: that is because the whale carried him off through the seas, cutting through them, until it reached the bottom of the sea. Yunus heard the glorifying of the pebbles at its floor, and at that moment and there he said: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You.﴾

Awf said: When Yunus was in the belly of the whale, he thought he had died. Then he moved his legs, and when they moved he prostrated in that place, then he called out: "O Lord, I have taken for You a place of worship in a spot where no one has taken one before."

Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri said: he remained in the belly of the whale for forty days. Both reports were narrated by Ibn Jubayr.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said, from one who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', the freedman of Umm Salamah: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah wished to imprison Yunus in the belly of the whale, He revealed to the whale: Take him, but do not scratch his flesh nor break his bone. When it brought him to the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself: What is this? Allah revealed to him, while he was in the belly of the whale: This is the glorification of the creatures of the sea. So he glorified Allah while in the belly of the whale, and the angels heard his glorification and said: O our Lord, we hear a faint sound in a strange land. He said: That is My servant Yunus, who disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the whale in the sea. They said: The righteous servant whose righteous deeds ascended to You every day and night? He said: Yes." He said: "Then they interceded for him, so He commanded the whale and it cast him onto the shore, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿while he was sick﴾ [As-Saffat: 145]."

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, through Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, and mentioned it in similar form, then said: "We do not know this to be narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through this route and this chain." Ibn Abd al-Haqq narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, from Ali, raised: "It is not befitting for a servant to say: 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'" He glorified Allah in the darknesses.

This hadith has also been narrated without this addition, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and Abdullah ibn Ja'far, and its chains will come in Surat Nun.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Akhi Ibn Wahb narrated to us, my paternal uncle narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, that Yazid al-Raqqashi narrated to him, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik, and I do not know except that Anas raised the hadith to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that Yunus the Prophet, peace be upon him, when it occurred to him to supplicate with these words while in the belly of the whale, said: "O Allah, there is no deity except You, glory be to You, indeed I have been of the wrongdoers." Then this supplication came circling around the Throne, and the angels said: O Lord, a faint voice known from a strange land? He said: Do you not recognize it? They said: No, O Lord, and who is it? He said: My servant Yunus. They said: Your servant Yunus, whose good deeds are always raised to You accepted, and whose supplications are answered? He said: Yes. They said: O Lord, will You not have mercy on what he used to do in ease, and rescue him from affliction? He said: Yes. Then He commanded the whale and it cast him onto the open land.

* *

His saying: ﴿So We answered him and rescued him from the distress﴾, meaning: We brought him out from the belly of the whale and those darknesses. ﴿And thus do We save the believers﴾, meaning: when they are in hardships and call upon Us turning to Us in repentance, and especially when they supplicate with this supplication in a time of affliction. The encouragement to supplicate with it has come from the master of the prophets. Imam Ahmad said:

Ismail ibn Umar narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, my father Muhammad narrated to me from his father Sa'd, that is Ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: I passed by Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, in the mosque, and I greeted him, but he looked at me and did not return my greeting. So I went to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: O Commander of the Faithful, has anything new happened in Islam? Twice. He said: No, what is it? I said: Only that I passed by Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, a moment ago in the mosque, and I greeted him, and he looked at me and did not return my greeting. He said: So Umar sent for Uthman and summoned him, and said: What prevented you from returning your brother's greeting? He said: I did not. Sa'd said: I said: Yes, you did, until he swore and I swore. Then Uthman remembered and said: Yes, I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. You passed by me just now while I was thinking to myself of a word I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Allah, I never recall it except that a veil covers my sight and my heart. Sa'd said: I will tell you of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned to us [the first supplication], then a Bedouin came and occupied him, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and I followed him. When I feared he would reach his house before me, I struck the ground with my foot. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to me and said: "Who is this? Abu Ishaq?" I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "What is it?" I said: No, by Allah, except that you mentioned to us the first supplication, then this Bedouin came and occupied you. He said: "Yes, the supplication of Dhu'n-Nun, when he was in the belly of the whale: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾. No Muslim has ever supplicated with it to his Lord for anything except that He answered him."

Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in "Amal al-Yawm wa'l-Laylah" narrated it through Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Sa'd, with the same wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Zayd, from al-Muttalib ibn Hantab (Abu Khalid said: I think he narrated from Mus'ab, meaning Ibn Sa'd), from Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever supplicates with the supplication of Yunus will have it answered." Abu Sa'id said: He means by it: ﴿And thus do We save the believers﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kalla'i narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Mansur narrated to me, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn Malik, that is Ibn Abi Waqqas, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Name of Allah by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives, is the supplication of Yunus ibn Matta." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it specific to Yunus alone, or is it for the community of the Muslims?" He said: "It is specific to Yunus ibn Matta, and general for the believers too, whenever they call upon it. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So he called out in the darknesses, 'There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.' So We answered him and saved him from the distress, and thus do We save the believers﴾? So it is a condition set by Allah for whoever calls upon Him with it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar ibn Qahdham al-Maqdisi narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Ma'bad, who said: I asked al-Hasan, I said: "O Abu Sa'id, is the Greatest Name of Allah the one by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives?" He said: "My nephew, do you not recite the Qur'an? The saying of Allah: ﴿And Dhu'n-Nun, when he went off in anger﴾, up to His saying: ﴿the believers﴾. My nephew, this is the Greatest Name of Allah, by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives."

[[Surat as-Saffat, verses 139-148, and Surat Nun (al-Qalam), verses 48-50.]] The reason is that Allah sent Yunus ibn Matta, peace be upon him, to the people of the town of Nineveh, which is a town in the land of Mosul. Then they humbled themselves before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and cried out to Him, and the camels bellowed with their young, the cows lowed with their calves, and the sheep bleated with their lambs. So Allah removed the punishment from them. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith would benefit it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world, and We let them enjoy for a time.﴾ [Yunus: 98].

As for Yunus, peace be upon him, he went and boarded a ship with some people, and the ship was tossed by the waves, and they feared they would drown. They cast lots over a man from among them to throw overboard, so that they could lighten the ship, and the lot fell upon Yunus. They refused to throw him, then they repeated the lot and it fell upon him again, and they refused. Then they repeated it and it fell upon him again. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So he drew lots and was among the losers﴾ [As-Saffat: 141], meaning the lot fell upon him. Yunus, peace be upon him, stood up, stripped off his clothes, and threw himself into the sea. Allah, glorified and exalted, had sent from the Green Sea, as Ibn Mas'ud said, a whale that cuts through the seas, and it came and swallowed Yunus when he threw himself from the ship. Allah revealed to that whale that it should not eat his flesh nor break his bones; for Yunus is not provision for you, rather your belly is a prison for him.

* *

His saying: ﴿Dhu'n-Nun﴾ means the whale; the attribution to it is correct on this basis.

* *

His saying: ﴿when he went off in anger﴾: al-Dahhak said, "to his people." ﴿So he thought that We would not decree against him﴾ [meaning: that We would not constrict him in the belly of the whale. This is reported similarly from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak and others, and Ibn Jarir chose it, citing as evidence the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And whoever has his provision restricted, let him spend from what Allah has given him. Allah does not burden a soul beyond what He has given it. Allah will bring about ease after hardship﴾ (At-Talaq: 7).

Ata al-Awfi said: ﴿So he thought that We would not decree against him﴾, meaning, "We would not decree (qadha) against him." It seems he took this to mean "qaddara" (to decree), since the Arabs say qadara and qaddara with the same meaning. A poet said: "Never shall that time that has passed return... Blessed are you; whatever you decree, will be; to you belongs the command..."

From this is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then the waters met for a matter already decreed﴾ [Al-Qamar: 12], meaning, it was decreed (quddira).

* *

His saying: ﴿So he called out in the darknesses: "There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers."﴾ Ibn Mas'ud said: the darkness of the belly of the whale, the darkness of the sea, and the darkness of the night. Similarly it was reported from Ibn Abbas, Amr ibn Maymun, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan and Qatadah.

Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd said: the darkness of a whale within the belly of another whale, in the darkness of the sea.

Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas and others said: that is because the whale carried him off through the seas, cutting through them, until it reached the bottom of the sea. Yunus heard the glorifying of the pebbles at its floor, and at that moment and there he said: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You.﴾

Awf said: When Yunus was in the belly of the whale, he thought he had died. Then he moved his legs, and when they moved he prostrated in that place, then he called out: "O Lord, I have taken for You a place of worship in a spot where no one has taken one before."

Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan al-Basri said: he remained in the belly of the whale for forty days. Both reports were narrated by Ibn Jubayr.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar said, from one who narrated to him, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', the freedman of Umm Salamah: I heard Abu Hurayrah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah wished to imprison Yunus in the belly of the whale, He revealed to the whale: Take him, but do not scratch his flesh nor break his bone. When it brought him to the bottom of the sea, Yunus heard a sound and said to himself: What is this? Allah revealed to him, while he was in the belly of the whale: This is the glorification of the creatures of the sea. So he glorified Allah while in the belly of the whale, and the angels heard his glorification and said: O our Lord, we hear a faint sound in a strange land. He said: That is My servant Yunus, who disobeyed Me, so I imprisoned him in the belly of the whale in the sea. They said: The righteous servant whose righteous deeds ascended to You every day and night? He said: Yes." He said: "Then they interceded for him, so He commanded the whale and it cast him onto the shore, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿while he was sick﴾ [As-Saffat: 145]."

Ibn Jarir narrated it. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad, through Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn Rafi', from Abu Hurayrah, and mentioned it in similar form, then said: "We do not know this to be narrated from the Prophet ﷺ except through this route and this chain." Ibn Abd al-Haqq narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Abdullah ibn Salamah, from Ali, raised: "It is not befitting for a servant to say: 'I am better than Yunus ibn Matta.'" He glorified Allah in the darknesses.

This hadith has also been narrated without this addition, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, Ibn Mas'ud and Abdullah ibn Ja'far, and its chains will come in Surat Nun.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Akhi Ibn Wahb narrated to us, my paternal uncle narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, that Yazid al-Raqqashi narrated to him, saying: I heard Anas ibn Malik, and I do not know except that Anas raised the hadith to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that Yunus the Prophet, peace be upon him, when it occurred to him to supplicate with these words while in the belly of the whale, said: "O Allah, there is no deity except You, glory be to You, indeed I have been of the wrongdoers." Then this supplication came circling around the Throne, and the angels said: O Lord, a faint voice known from a strange land? He said: Do you not recognize it? They said: No, O Lord, and who is it? He said: My servant Yunus. They said: Your servant Yunus, whose good deeds are always raised to You accepted, and whose supplications are answered? He said: Yes. They said: O Lord, will You not have mercy on what he used to do in ease, and rescue him from affliction? He said: Yes. Then He commanded the whale and it cast him onto the open land.

* *

His saying: ﴿So We answered him and rescued him from the distress﴾, meaning: We brought him out from the belly of the whale and those darknesses. ﴿And thus do We save the believers﴾, meaning: when they are in hardships and call upon Us turning to Us in repentance, and especially when they supplicate with this supplication in a time of affliction. The encouragement to supplicate with it has come from the master of the prophets. Imam Ahmad said:

Ismail ibn Umar narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, my father Muhammad narrated to me from his father Sa'd, that is Ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: I passed by Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, in the mosque, and I greeted him, but he looked at me and did not return my greeting. So I went to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: O Commander of the Faithful, has anything new happened in Islam? Twice. He said: No, what is it? I said: Only that I passed by Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, a moment ago in the mosque, and I greeted him, and he looked at me and did not return my greeting. He said: So Umar sent for Uthman and summoned him, and said: What prevented you from returning your brother's greeting? He said: I did not. Sa'd said: I said: Yes, you did, until he swore and I swore. Then Uthman remembered and said: Yes, I seek Allah's forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance. You passed by me just now while I was thinking to myself of a word I heard from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. By Allah, I never recall it except that a veil covers my sight and my heart. Sa'd said: I will tell you of it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned to us [the first supplication], then a Bedouin came and occupied him, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, and I followed him. When I feared he would reach his house before me, I struck the ground with my foot. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned to me and said: "Who is this? Abu Ishaq?" I said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: "What is it?" I said: No, by Allah, except that you mentioned to us the first supplication, then this Bedouin came and occupied you. He said: "Yes, the supplication of Dhu'n-Nun, when he was in the belly of the whale: ﴿There is no deity except You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers﴾. No Muslim has ever supplicated with it to his Lord for anything except that He answered him."

Al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i in "Amal al-Yawm wa'l-Laylah" narrated it through Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from his father, from Sa'd, with the same wording.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Zayd, from al-Muttalib ibn Hantab (Abu Khalid said: I think he narrated from Mus'ab, meaning Ibn Sa'd), from Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever supplicates with the supplication of Yunus will have it answered." Abu Sa'id said: He means by it: ﴿And thus do We save the believers﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kalla'i narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn Mansur narrated to me, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn Malik, that is Ibn Abi Waqqas, saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The Name of Allah by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives, is the supplication of Yunus ibn Matta." He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, is it specific to Yunus alone, or is it for the community of the Muslims?" He said: "It is specific to Yunus ibn Matta, and general for the believers too, whenever they call upon it. Have you not heard the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So he called out in the darknesses, 'There is no god but You; glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.' So We answered him and saved him from the distress, and thus do We save the believers﴾? So it is a condition set by Allah for whoever calls upon Him with it."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Suraij narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar ibn Qahdham al-Maqdisi narrated to us, from Kathir ibn Ma'bad, who said: I asked al-Hasan, I said: "O Abu Sa'id, is the Greatest Name of Allah the one by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives?" He said: "My nephew, do you not recite the Qur'an? The saying of Allah: ﴿And Dhu'n-Nun, when he went off in anger﴾, up to His saying: ﴿the believers﴾. My nephew, this is the Greatest Name of Allah, by which, when He is called upon, He answers, and when He is asked by it, He gives."

The Most High informs us about His servant Zakariyya, when he asked that Allah grant him a child who would be a prophet after him. The story has already been presented in full at the beginning of Surah Maryam and also in Surah Al 'Imran, and here it is more concise than in those two places. ﴿When he called out to his Lord﴾, meaning secretly, away from his people: ﴿My Lord, do not leave me alone (without an heir)﴾, meaning I have no child and no heir who will stand after me among the people. ﴿And You are the best of inheritors﴾ is a supplication and a praise appropriate to the request.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So We responded to him and granted him Yahya, and We made his wife fit for him﴾, meaning, his wife.

Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: she was barren and could not bear children, and then she gave birth.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi [in t: "Ibn Munabbih"] narrated from Talhah ibn 'Amr, from 'Ata': there was a length in her tongue, and Allah made it right. In another narration: there was something in her physique, and Allah made it right. Muhammad ibn Ka'b and al-Suddi said the same. The first view is more apparent from the context.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds﴾, meaning, in performing acts of nearness to Allah and in carrying out acts of obedience, ﴿and they would call upon Us with hope and fear﴾. al-Thawri said: ﴿with hope﴾ for what is with Us, and ﴿with fear﴾ of what is with Us. ﴿And they were humbly submissive to Us﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: meaning, believing in what Allah has sent down. Mujahid said: truly believing. Abu al-'Aliyah said: fearful. Abu Sinan said: khushu' is the fear that settles in the heart and never leaves it. Also from Mujahid: ﴿khashi'in﴾ means humble. al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Dahhak said: ﴿khashi'in﴾ means submissive before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. All these statements are close in meaning.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us; 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us; 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq ibn 'Abd Allah al-Qurashi narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn Hakim, who said: Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) addressed us, then said: "To proceed: I advise you to have taqwa of Allah, to praise Him with what He is worthy of, to combine hope with fear, and to combine insistence in supplication with asking. Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, praised Zakariyya and his family, saying: ﴿Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds, and they would call upon Us with hope and fear, and they were humbly submissive to Us﴾."

Thus Allah, the Exalted, links the story of Maryam and her son ʿĪsā, peace be upon them, with the story of Zakariyya and his son Yahya, peace be upon them both. He mentions the story of Zakariyya first and then follows it with the story of Maryam, because the former is a preparation for the latter. For the former is the bringing about of a child from an aged old man who had advanced in years, and from an old woman who was barren and had not borne children in her youth. Then He mentions the story of Maryam, which is more astonishing, for it is the bringing about of a child from a female without a male. This is how it occurs in Surah Āl ʿImrān and in Surah Maryam, and here He mentioned the story of Zakariyya and then followed it with the story of Maryam. So His saying ﴿and she who guarded her chastity﴾ refers to Maryam, peace be upon her, as He said in Surah al-Tahrim: ﴿And Maryam, the daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into it of Our Spirit﴾ [al-Tahrim: 12].

* *

His saying ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾ means: a proof that Allah is over all things capable, and that He creates what He wills, and ﴿His command, when He intends a thing, is only that He says to it, "Be," and it is﴾ [Yasin: 82]. This is like His saying: ﴿and that We may make him a sign for people﴾ [Maryam: 21].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, Abu ʿĀsim al-Ḍaḥḥāk ibn Mukhallad narrated to us, from Shabīb (i.e., Ibn Bishr), from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿for the worlds﴾, he said: "The worlds" are the jinn and mankind.

Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾: "Your religion is one religion."

Al-Hasan al-Basri said regarding this verse: "He clarified for them what they should fear and what they should do, then said: ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾," meaning: your sunnah is one sunnah. So His words ﴿Indeed, this﴾ are the particle inna (إِنَّ, indeed) and its noun, and ﴿community of yours﴾ is the predicate of inna, meaning: this is your sharia (sharīʿah, the divine law) which I have explained to you and made clear to you. His words ﴿one community﴾ are in the accusative as a state (ḥāl). For this reason He said: ﴿And I am your Lord, so worship Me﴾, just as He said: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds; indeed, I am Knowing of what you do. And indeed, this community of yours is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me﴾ [al-Muʾminun: 51–52]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "We, the company of the prophets, are sons of one father (ʿallāt); our religion is one." He means that the aim is the worship of Allah alone, with no partner, though the sharia given to His messengers varied, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿To each of you We have appointed a law (shirʿah) and a method (minhāj)﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48].

* *

His words ﴿but they divided their affair among themselves﴾ mean: the nations differed concerning their messengers, some affirming them and some denying them. For this reason He said: ﴿To Us they will all return﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, when each will be recompensed according to his deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. For this reason He said: ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds while being a believer﴾, meaning his heart affirms and he does righteous deeds, ﴿his effort will not be denied﴾, like His words: ﴿Indeed, We do not waste the reward of one who does good work﴾ [al-Kahf: 30]. That is, his effort, which is his work, will not be rejected, but will be appreciated, so he will not be wronged even by the weight of an atom. For this reason He said: ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾, meaning all of his deeds are written, so nothing of them is lost to him.
