Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 21, verse 95–97 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is forbidden upon a city﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is decreed" (wajab), meaning: it is a predetermined decree (qadaran muqaddaran) that the people of every city that is destroyed will not return to the world before the Day of Resurrection. This was explicitly stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, Qatadah, and others.

In a narration from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿that they will not return﴾, meaning: they will not repent.

The first opinion is more apparent, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose﴾: We have already mentioned that they are from the progeny of Adam, peace be upon him. Indeed, they are also from the offspring of Noah, from the descendants of Yafith, father of the Turks, and the Turks are a remnant of them, who were left behind the barrier that Dhul-Qarnayn built.

And He said: ﴿This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true. And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them together in a gathering﴾ [al-Kahf 18:98–99]. And He said in this noble verse: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they come swarming down from every mound﴾, meaning: they hasten in their walking toward corruption.

Al-hadab: it is the elevated part of the earth, as stated by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih, al-Thawri, and others. This is their description at the time of their emergence, as if the listener were witnessing it. ﴿And none can inform you like the One who is All-Aware﴾ [Fatir 35:14]: this is the report of One who knows what has been and what will be, who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth; there is no god but Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: Ibn 'Abbas saw children leaping upon one another while playing, and Ibn 'Abbas said: "Thus will Gog and Magog emerge."

The mention of their emergence has come in several hadiths from the Prophetic Sunnah:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Gog and Magog will be let loose, and they will emerge as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿and they come swarming down from every mound﴾. They will overwhelm the people, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their cities and fortresses, and they will gather their livestock to themselves, and they will drink the waters of the earth, until some of them pass by a river and drink whatever is in it until they leave it dry. Then, when no one remains among the people except one in a fortress or a city, one of them will say: 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them. Only the people of the heaven remain.'" He said: "Then one of them will brandish his spear and throw it toward the sky, and it will return to him stained with blood, as a trial and a tribulation. While they are in that state, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send worms into their necks, like the locust's worm that emerges in its neck, and in the morning they will be dead, without any sound to be heard from them. The Muslims will say: 'Is there not a man who will sell himself for us and go and see what this enemy has done?'" He said: "A man from among them will strip himself, seeking reward, having resolved himself to be killed. He will descend and find them dead, some upon others. He will call out: 'O company of Muslims, rejoice! Allah the Mighty and Majestic has sufficed you against your enemy.' They will come out of their cities and fortresses, and they will send their livestock to graze, and their livestock will have no pasture except their flesh, and it will become fatter from it than it ever became from any plant it had ever eaten."

Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Ibn Ishaq, with the same chain. (Al-Musnad (3/77) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4079). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/260): "This chain is sound, and its narrators are trustworthy.")

The second hadith: Imam Ahmad also said: al-Walid ibn Muslim Abu al-'Abbas al-Dimashqi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to us, Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, the judge of Homs, narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami narrated to me, from his father, that he heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Kilabi say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the Dajjal one morning, and he lowered his voice regarding him and raised it, until we thought he was in the group of palm trees. When we went to him, he perceived that in our faces, so we asked him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you mentioned the Dajjal this morning, and you lowered your voice and raised it until we thought he was in the group of palm trees." He said: "Other than the Dajjal, I fear for you more. If he emerges while I am among you, I will be his opponent on your behalf, and if he emerges while I am not among you, each man will be his own opponent, and Allah is my successor over every Muslim. He is a young man with curly hair, his eye bulging. He will emerge between al-Sham and Iraq and will spread corruption to the right and to the left. O servants of Allah, stand firm."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, how long will he remain on the earth?" He said: "Forty days: one day like a year, one day like a month, one day like a week, and the rest of his days are like your days."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, on that day which is like a year, will the prayer of one day and night suffice us in it?" He said: "No; estimate its measure."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is his speed on the earth?" He said: "Like rain driven by the wind." He said: "He will pass by a people and call them, and they will respond to him, and he will command the sky and it will rain, and the earth and it will grow, and their grazing animals will return to them with humps longest, udders fullest, and flanks widest. And he will pass by a people and call them, and they will reject his word, and their wealth will follow him, and they will awake in drought, having nothing of their wealth. And he will pass by a ruin and say to it: 'Bring out your treasures,' and its treasures will follow him like swarms of bees." He said: "And he will order a man to be killed, and he will strike him with a sword and cut him into two pieces, the distance of a target's throw. Then he will call him, and he will come to him, his face radiant."

While they are in that state, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send the Messiah, son of Mary, and he will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, between two garments, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. He will pursue him and overtake him and kill him at the eastern gate of Lud.

He said: "While they are like that, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will reveal to 'Isa ibn Maryam: 'I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one has the power to fight. So bring My servants to Mount Tur.' Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send forth Gog and Magog, and they are as Allah said: ﴿from every mound they come swarming﴾. 'Isa and his companions will seek refuge in Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and Allah will send upon them a worm in their necks, and in the morning they will be dead, like the death of one soul."

Then 'Isa and his companions will descend, and they will find no house on the earth that has not been filled with their stench and their putrefaction. 'Isa and his companions will seek refuge in Allah, and He will send upon them birds like the necks of Bactrian camels, which will carry them and cast them wherever Allah wills."

Ibn Jarir said: 'Ata' ibn Yazid al-Saksaki narrated to me, from Ka'b, or someone else, who said: "They will be cast into al-Mahbal." [Ibn Jarir said: I said: "O Abu Yazid, where is al-Mahbal?"] He said: "The rising place of the sun."

He said: "And Allah will send a rain from which no house of clay or wool will be spared for forty days, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like a smooth stone, and it will be said to the earth: 'Bring forth your fruit and return your blessings.'" He said: "On that day a company will eat from a pomegranate and shelter beneath its husk, and the milk will be blessed, so that a she-camel's milk will suffice a large group of people, a cow's milk will suffice a clan, and a sheep's milk will suffice a household."

He said: "While they are in that state, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send a pleasant wind beneath their armpits, which will take the soul of every Muslim, or every believer, and the wicked of mankind will remain, copulating openly like donkeys, and upon them the Hour will be established."

Muslim alone recorded it, to the exclusion of al-Bukhari, and he narrated it along with the rest of the authors of the Sunan through several routes, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir. (Al-Musnad (4/181); Sahih Muslim no. (2137); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4321); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2240); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10783); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4075).) Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

The third hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Ibn Harmalah, from his maternal aunt, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon while his finger was bandaged from a scorpion sting, and he said: "You say: 'There is no enemy [for you],' and you will not cease fighting an enemy until Gog and Magog come, broad-faced, small-eyed, with reddish hair, coming swarming from every mound, as if their faces were hammered shields."

Ibn Abi Hatim similarly narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Harmalah al-Mudlaji, from an aunt of his, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned the like of it.

The fourth hadith: It has already passed in the tafsir of the end of Surat al-A'raf, from the narration of Imam Ahmad, from Hushaym, from al-'Awwam, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Mu'thir ibn 'Afazah, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa, peace be upon them." He said: "They discussed the matter of the Hour, and they referred their matter to Ibrahim, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' Then they referred their matter to Musa, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' Then they referred their matter to 'Isa, and he said: 'As for its appointed time, no one knows it except Allah, and my Lord has covenanted with me that the Dajjal will emerge.'"

He said: "And with me are two staves, and when he sees me, he will melt as lead melts." He said: "Allah will destroy him when he sees me, so much so that the stone and the tree will say: 'O Muslim, there is a disbeliever beneath me, so come and kill him.'" He said: "Allah will destroy them, then the people will return to their lands and homelands." He said: "At that time Gog and Magog will emerge, and they are from every mound coming swarming, and they will trample their lands, and they will not come upon anything without destroying it, and they will not pass by any water without drinking it." He said: "Then the people will return to me complaining of them, and I will supplicate Allah against them, and He will destroy them and cause them to die, until the earth reeks from the stench of them, and Allah will send rain that will sweep away their bodies, until it casts them into the sea. Regarding what my Lord has covenanted with me: when that occurs, the Hour will be like a pregnant woman near her time, whose family does not know when she will surprise them with her delivery, by night or by day."

Ibn Majah narrated it from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Yazid ibn Harun, from al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab, with its like, and he added: "Al-'Awwam said: 'And the confirmation of that has been found in the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they come swarming down from every mound﴾.'" (Al-Musnad (1/375); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4081); and it was mentioned previously at the tafsir of verse 187 of Surat al-A'raf.)

Ibn Jarir also narrated it here from the hadith of Jabalah, with it. (Tafsir al-Tabari (17/72).)

The hadiths on this subject are very numerous, and the reports from the early generations are likewise.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, through Ma'mar, from more than one narrator, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu al-Sayf, who said: Ka'b (al-Ahbar) said: "When the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj draws near, they will dig until those nearest to them can hear the clinking of their picks. When night falls they will say: 'Tomorrow we will come and break out.' Then Allah will restore it just as it was. So they come the next day and find that Allah has restored it just as it was, and they dig until those nearest to them can hear the clinking of their picks. When night falls, Allah will put into the tongue of one of them the words: 'Tomorrow we will come and break out, if Allah wills.' So they come the next day and find it just as they left it, and they dig until they emerge. The first group will pass by a lake and drink its water; then the second group will pass by and lick its mud; then the third group will pass by and say: 'There was water here once.' The people will flee from them, and nothing will be able to stand against them. Then they will shoot their arrows into the sky, and the arrows will return to them stained with blood, and they will say: 'We have overcome the people of the earth and the people of the heaven.' Then Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, will supplicate against them, saying: 'O Allah, we have no strength or power against them, so suffice us against them however You wish.' Allah will then send against them a worm called al-Naghf, which will pierce their necks, and Allah will send birds that will seize them in their beaks and cast them into the sea. Allah will send a spring called 'Al-Hayah' (the Life), by which Allah will purify the earth and make it grow, so that a pomegranate will be sufficient for a whole band of people to eat their fill of it, and they will shelter under its skin." It was said: "And what is al-Sakan, O Ka'b?" He said: "The household." He said: "While the people are in that state, there will come to them the cry that Dhu al-Suwayqatayn is coming against them. Then Isa ibn Maryam will send out an advance force of seven hundred, or between seven hundred and eight hundred. When they are in part of the way, Allah will send a pleasant southern wind, which will take the souls of every believer. Then only the worst of people will remain, and they will copulate in the open like beasts, and the Hour will come upon them like a man who circles his mare, waiting to see when she will give birth." Ka'b said: "Whoever goes beyond my words here with any speculation, or beyond my knowledge here with anything, then he is the one who over-reaches."

This is among the finest of the narrations of Ka'b al-Ahbar, because it is corroborated by authentic reports.

It has been established in a hadith that Isa ibn Maryam will perform Hajj to the Ancient House (al-Bayt al-'Atiq). Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abd Allah ibn Abi 'Utbah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This House will certainly be visited for Hajj and 'Umrah after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj." Al-Bukhari alone recorded it. [Al-Musnad (3/27) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1593.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the true promise draws near﴾, it means the Day of Resurrection. When these terrors, earthquakes and calamities occur, the Hour has drawn near and approached. When it has come and occurred, the disbelievers will say: ﴿This is a difficult day﴾ [Al-Qamar: 8]. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾, meaning, because of the severity of the great matters they witness: ﴿O woe to us!﴾, that is, they will say: ﴿O woe to us! We were heedless of this﴾, meaning in the world, ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾, acknowledging their wrongdoing against themselves, but this will not benefit them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 21, verse 95–97 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is forbidden upon a city﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is decreed" (wajab), meaning: it is a predetermined decree (qadaran muqaddaran) that the people of every city that is destroyed will not return to the world before the Day of Resurrection. This was explicitly stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, Qatadah, and others.

In a narration from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿that they will not return﴾, meaning: they will not repent.

The first opinion is more apparent, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose﴾: We have already mentioned that they are from the progeny of Adam, peace be upon him. Indeed, they are also from the offspring of Noah, from the descendants of Yafith, father of the Turks, and the Turks are a remnant of them, who were left behind the barrier that Dhul-Qarnayn built.

And He said: ﴿This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true. And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them together in a gathering﴾ [al-Kahf 18:98–99]. And He said in this noble verse: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they come swarming down from every mound﴾, meaning: they hasten in their walking toward corruption.

Al-hadab: it is the elevated part of the earth, as stated by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih, al-Thawri, and others. This is their description at the time of their emergence, as if the listener were witnessing it. ﴿And none can inform you like the One who is All-Aware﴾ [Fatir 35:14]: this is the report of One who knows what has been and what will be, who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth; there is no god but Him.

Then Isa ibn Maryam will send out an advance force of seven hundred, or between seven hundred and eight hundred. When they are in part of the way, Allah will send a pleasant southern wind, which will take the souls of every believer. Then only the worst of people will remain, and they will copulate in the open like beasts, and the Hour will come upon them like a man who circles his mare, waiting to see when she will give birth." Ka'b said: "Whoever goes beyond my words here with any speculation, or beyond my knowledge here with anything, then he is the one who over-reaches."

This is among the finest of the narrations of Ka'b al-Ahbar, because it is corroborated by authentic reports.

It has been established in a hadith that Isa ibn Maryam will perform Hajj to the Ancient House (al-Bayt al-'Atiq). Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abd Allah ibn Abi 'Utbah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This House will certainly be visited for Hajj and 'Umrah after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj." Al-Bukhari alone recorded it. [Al-Musnad (3/27) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1593.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the true promise draws near﴾, it means the Day of Resurrection. When these terrors, earthquakes and calamities occur, the Hour has drawn near and approached. When it has come and occurred, the disbelievers will say: ﴿This is a difficult day﴾ [Al-Qamar: 8]. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾, meaning, because of the severity of the great matters they witness: ﴿O woe to us!﴾, that is, they will say: ﴿O woe to us! We were heedless of this﴾, meaning in the world, ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾, acknowledging their wrongdoing against themselves, but this will not benefit them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 21, verse 95–97 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it is forbidden upon a city﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is decreed" (wajab), meaning: it is a predetermined decree (qadaran muqaddaran) that the people of every city that is destroyed will not return to the world before the Day of Resurrection. This was explicitly stated by Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, Qatadah, and others.

In a narration from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿that they will not return﴾, meaning: they will not repent.

The first opinion is more apparent, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose﴾: We have already mentioned that they are from the progeny of Adam, peace be upon him. Indeed, they are also from the offspring of Noah, from the descendants of Yafith, father of the Turks, and the Turks are a remnant of them, who were left behind the barrier that Dhul-Qarnayn built.

And He said: ﴿This is a mercy from my Lord; but when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, and the promise of my Lord is ever true. And We will leave some of them that day surging over one another, and the Horn will be blown, and We will gather them together in a gathering﴾ [al-Kahf 18:98–99]. And He said in this noble verse: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they come swarming down from every mound﴾, meaning: they hasten in their walking toward corruption.

Al-hadab: it is the elevated part of the earth, as stated by Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih, al-Thawri, and others. This is their description at the time of their emergence, as if the listener were witnessing it. ﴿And none can inform you like the One who is All-Aware﴾ [Fatir 35:14]: this is the report of One who knows what has been and what will be, who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth; there is no god but Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who said: Ibn 'Abbas saw children leaping upon one another while playing, and Ibn 'Abbas said: "Thus will Gog and Magog emerge."

The mention of their emergence has come in several hadiths from the Prophetic Sunnah:

The first hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from Mahmud ibn Labid, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Gog and Magog will be let loose, and they will emerge as Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿and they come swarming down from every mound﴾. They will overwhelm the people, and the Muslims will withdraw from them to their cities and fortresses, and they will gather their livestock to themselves, and they will drink the waters of the earth, until some of them pass by a river and drink whatever is in it until they leave it dry. Then, when no one remains among the people except one in a fortress or a city, one of them will say: 'These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them. Only the people of the heaven remain.'" He said: "Then one of them will brandish his spear and throw it toward the sky, and it will return to him stained with blood, as a trial and a tribulation. While they are in that state, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send worms into their necks, like the locust's worm that emerges in its neck, and in the morning they will be dead, without any sound to be heard from them. The Muslims will say: 'Is there not a man who will sell himself for us and go and see what this enemy has done?'" He said: "A man from among them will strip himself, seeking reward, having resolved himself to be killed. He will descend and find them dead, some upon others. He will call out: 'O company of Muslims, rejoice! Allah the Mighty and Majestic has sufficed you against your enemy.' They will come out of their cities and fortresses, and they will send their livestock to graze, and their livestock will have no pasture except their flesh, and it will become fatter from it than it ever became from any plant it had ever eaten."

Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Yunus ibn Bukayr, from Ibn Ishaq, with the same chain. (Al-Musnad (3/77) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4079). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/260): "This chain is sound, and its narrators are trustworthy.")

The second hadith: Imam Ahmad also said: al-Walid ibn Muslim Abu al-'Abbas al-Dimashqi narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir narrated to us, Yahya ibn Jabir al-Ta'i, the judge of Homs, narrated to me, 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr al-Hadrami narrated to me, from his father, that he heard al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an al-Kilabi say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the Dajjal one morning, and he lowered his voice regarding him and raised it, until we thought he was in the group of palm trees. When we went to him, he perceived that in our faces, so we asked him and said: "O Messenger of Allah, you mentioned the Dajjal this morning, and you lowered your voice and raised it until we thought he was in the group of palm trees." He said: "Other than the Dajjal, I fear for you more. If he emerges while I am among you, I will be his opponent on your behalf, and if he emerges while I am not among you, each man will be his own opponent, and Allah is my successor over every Muslim. He is a young man with curly hair, his eye bulging. He will emerge between al-Sham and Iraq and will spread corruption to the right and to the left. O servants of Allah, stand firm."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, how long will he remain on the earth?" He said: "Forty days: one day like a year, one day like a month, one day like a week, and the rest of his days are like your days."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, on that day which is like a year, will the prayer of one day and night suffice us in it?" He said: "No; estimate its measure."

We said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is his speed on the earth?" He said: "Like rain driven by the wind." He said: "He will pass by a people and call them, and they will respond to him, and he will command the sky and it will rain, and the earth and it will grow, and their grazing animals will return to them with humps longest, udders fullest, and flanks widest. And he will pass by a people and call them, and they will reject his word, and their wealth will follow him, and they will awake in drought, having nothing of their wealth. And he will pass by a ruin and say to it: 'Bring out your treasures,' and its treasures will follow him like swarms of bees." He said: "And he will order a man to be killed, and he will strike him with a sword and cut him into two pieces, the distance of a target's throw. Then he will call him, and he will come to him, his face radiant."

While they are in that state, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send the Messiah, son of Mary, and he will descend at the white minaret east of Damascus, between two garments, placing his hands on the wings of two angels. He will pursue him and overtake him and kill him at the eastern gate of Lud.

He said: "While they are like that, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will reveal to 'Isa ibn Maryam: 'I have brought forth servants of Mine whom no one has the power to fight. So bring My servants to Mount Tur.' Then Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send forth Gog and Magog, and they are as Allah said: ﴿from every mound they come swarming﴾. 'Isa and his companions will seek refuge in Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and Allah will send upon them a worm in their necks, and in the morning they will be dead, like the death of one soul."

Then 'Isa and his companions will descend, and they will find no house on the earth that has not been filled with their stench and their putrefaction. 'Isa and his companions will seek refuge in Allah, and He will send upon them birds like the necks of Bactrian camels, which will carry them and cast them wherever Allah wills."

Ibn Jarir said: 'Ata' ibn Yazid al-Saksaki narrated to me, from Ka'b, or someone else, who said: "They will be cast into al-Mahbal." [Ibn Jarir said: I said: "O Abu Yazid, where is al-Mahbal?"] He said: "The rising place of the sun."

He said: "And Allah will send a rain from which no house of clay or wool will be spared for forty days, and it will wash the earth until it leaves it like a smooth stone, and it will be said to the earth: 'Bring forth your fruit and return your blessings.'" He said: "On that day a company will eat from a pomegranate and shelter beneath its husk, and the milk will be blessed, so that a she-camel's milk will suffice a large group of people, a cow's milk will suffice a clan, and a sheep's milk will suffice a household."

He said: "While they are in that state, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will send a pleasant wind beneath their armpits, which will take the soul of every Muslim, or every believer, and the wicked of mankind will remain, copulating openly like donkeys, and upon them the Hour will be established."

Muslim alone recorded it, to the exclusion of al-Bukhari, and he narrated it along with the rest of the authors of the Sunan through several routes, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir. (Al-Musnad (4/181); Sahih Muslim no. (2137); Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4321); Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2240); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10783); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4075).) Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih."

The third hadith: Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, from Ibn Harmalah, from his maternal aunt, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) delivered a sermon while his finger was bandaged from a scorpion sting, and he said: "You say: 'There is no enemy [for you],' and you will not cease fighting an enemy until Gog and Magog come, broad-faced, small-eyed, with reddish hair, coming swarming from every mound, as if their faces were hammered shields."

Ibn Abi Hatim similarly narrated it from the hadith of Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Harmalah al-Mudlaji, from an aunt of his, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and he mentioned the like of it.

The fourth hadith: It has already passed in the tafsir of the end of Surat al-A'raf, from the narration of Imam Ahmad, from Hushaym, from al-'Awwam, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Mu'thir ibn 'Afazah, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I met Ibrahim, Musa, and 'Isa, peace be upon them." He said: "They discussed the matter of the Hour, and they referred their matter to Ibrahim, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' Then they referred their matter to Musa, and he said: 'I have no knowledge of it.' Then they referred their matter to 'Isa, and he said: 'As for its appointed time, no one knows it except Allah, and my Lord has covenanted with me that the Dajjal will emerge.'"

He said: "And with me are two staves, and when he sees me, he will melt as lead melts." He said: "Allah will destroy him when he sees me, so much so that the stone and the tree will say: 'O Muslim, there is a disbeliever beneath me, so come and kill him.'" He said: "Allah will destroy them, then the people will return to their lands and homelands." He said: "At that time Gog and Magog will emerge, and they are from every mound coming swarming, and they will trample their lands, and they will not come upon anything without destroying it, and they will not pass by any water without drinking it." He said: "Then the people will return to me complaining of them, and I will supplicate Allah against them, and He will destroy them and cause them to die, until the earth reeks from the stench of them, and Allah will send rain that will sweep away their bodies, until it casts them into the sea. Regarding what my Lord has covenanted with me: when that occurs, the Hour will be like a pregnant woman near her time, whose family does not know when she will surprise them with her delivery, by night or by day."

Ibn Majah narrated it from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, from Yazid ibn Harun, from al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab, with its like, and he added: "Al-'Awwam said: 'And the confirmation of that has been found in the Book of Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they come swarming down from every mound﴾.'" (Al-Musnad (1/375); Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4081); and it was mentioned previously at the tafsir of verse 187 of Surat al-A'raf.)

Ibn Jarir also narrated it here from the hadith of Jabalah, with it. (Tafsir al-Tabari (17/72).)

The hadiths on this subject are very numerous, and the reports from the early generations are likewise.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, through Ma'mar, from more than one narrator, from Humayd ibn Hilal, from Abu al-Sayf, who said: Ka'b (al-Ahbar) said: "When the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj draws near, they will dig until those nearest to them can hear the clinking of their picks. When night falls they will say: 'Tomorrow we will come and break out.' Then Allah will restore it just as it was. So they come the next day and find that Allah has restored it just as it was, and they dig until those nearest to them can hear the clinking of their picks. When night falls, Allah will put into the tongue of one of them the words: 'Tomorrow we will come and break out, if Allah wills.' So they come the next day and find it just as they left it, and they dig until they emerge. The first group will pass by a lake and drink its water; then the second group will pass by and lick its mud; then the third group will pass by and say: 'There was water here once.' The people will flee from them, and nothing will be able to stand against them. Then they will shoot their arrows into the sky, and the arrows will return to them stained with blood, and they will say: 'We have overcome the people of the earth and the people of the heaven.' Then Isa ibn Maryam, peace be upon him, will supplicate against them, saying: 'O Allah, we have no strength or power against them, so suffice us against them however You wish.' Allah will then send against them a worm called al-Naghf, which will pierce their necks, and Allah will send birds that will seize them in their beaks and cast them into the sea. Allah will send a spring called 'Al-Hayah' (the Life), by which Allah will purify the earth and make it grow, so that a pomegranate will be sufficient for a whole band of people to eat their fill of it, and they will shelter under its skin." It was said: "And what is al-Sakan, O Ka'b?" He said: "The household." He said: "While the people are in that state, there will come to them the cry that Dhu al-Suwayqatayn is coming against them. Then Isa ibn Maryam will send out an advance force of seven hundred, or between seven hundred and eight hundred. When they are in part of the way, Allah will send a pleasant southern wind, which will take the souls of every believer. Then only the worst of people will remain, and they will copulate in the open like beasts, and the Hour will come upon them like a man who circles his mare, waiting to see when she will give birth." Ka'b said: "Whoever goes beyond my words here with any speculation, or beyond my knowledge here with anything, then he is the one who over-reaches."

This is among the finest of the narrations of Ka'b al-Ahbar, because it is corroborated by authentic reports.

It has been established in a hadith that Isa ibn Maryam will perform Hajj to the Ancient House (al-Bayt al-'Atiq). Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Dawud narrated to us, Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abd Allah ibn Abi 'Utbah, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "This House will certainly be visited for Hajj and 'Umrah after the emergence of Ya'juj and Ma'juj." Al-Bukhari alone recorded it. [Al-Musnad (3/27) and Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1593.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the true promise draws near﴾, it means the Day of Resurrection. When these terrors, earthquakes and calamities occur, the Hour has drawn near and approached. When it has come and occurred, the disbelievers will say: ﴿This is a difficult day﴾ [Al-Qamar: 8]. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then, behold, the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare fixedly﴾, meaning, because of the severity of the great matters they witness: ﴿O woe to us!﴾, that is, they will say: ﴿O woe to us! We were heedless of this﴾, meaning in the world, ﴿Rather, we were wrongdoers﴾, acknowledging their wrongdoing against themselves, but this will not benefit them.

He (Allah) says, addressing the people of Makkah among the polytheists of Quraysh and those who followed their religion from among the worshippers of idols and images:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, its fuel, as in His saying: ﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6].

Ibn 'Abbas also said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means the trees of Hell. In another narration he said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means the firewood of Hell, in the Zanji language (the language of the Zanj).

Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: its firewood. This is also how it is read in the qira'a (variant recitation) of 'Ali and 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means what is thrown into it.

Others said similarly. All these meanings are close to one another.

* *

His saying: ﴿You are to enter it﴾ means: you will enter it.

﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it﴾: that is, if these idols and rivals which you have taken besides Allah were true gods, they would not have entered the Fire, nor would they have gone into it. ﴿And all will abide therein forever﴾: that is, the worshippers and what they worshipped, all of them will abide in it forever. ﴿For them therein is groaning﴾, as He said: ﴿For them therein is groaning and wailing﴾ [Hud: 106]. Al-zafir is the expulsion of their breaths, and al-shahiq is the drawing in of their breaths. ﴿And they therein will not hear﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman (i.e. al-Mas'udi) narrated to us, from his father, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: When there remain those who will abide forever in the Fire, they will be placed in coffins of fire, with nails of fire, so that none of them will see that anyone else is being punished in the Fire. Then 'Abdullah recited: ﴿For them therein is groaning, and they therein will not hear﴾.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from al-Mas'udi, from Yunus ibn Khabbab [in T: "Ibn Hibban"], from Ibn Mas'ud, and he mentioned it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾: 'Ikrimah said: the mercy. Others said: the happiness. ﴿Those will be kept far from it﴾. When Allah mentioned the people of the Fire and their punishment because of their associating partners with Allah, He followed it with mention of the happy among the believers in Allah and His messengers [in T: "messenger"], those for whom happiness had preceded from Allah, and who sent forward righteous deeds in this world, as He said: ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26], and He said: ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60]. Just as they did good in this world, Allah made their end and their reward good, so He saved them from the punishment and granted them abundant reward. He said: ﴿Those will be kept far from it. They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that is, its burning in the bodies.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Jurayri [in T, F, A: "from Abu 'Uthman al-Jurayri"], from Abu 'Uthman, regarding ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, he said: there are serpents on the Path (al-Sirat) that sting them, and when they are stung, he says: "Hass, hass" [an exclamation of pain].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they, in what their souls desire, will abide forever﴾: He saved them from what is feared and dreaded, and they obtained what is sought and loved.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Yazid al-Hamdani narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from the paternal cousin of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: [he spent the night chatting with 'Ali one night, and he recited: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾, and he said: "I am among them, 'Umar is among them, 'Uthman is among them, al-Zubayr is among them, Talhah is among them, 'Abd al-Rahman is among them" or he said: "Sa'd is among them." He said: The prayer was established, so he stood up, and I think he was dragging his garment, and he was saying: ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾.

Shu'bah said, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf al-Makki, from Muhammad ibn Hatib [in T: "Khatib"], who said: I heard 'Ali say regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾: "'Uthman and his companions."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Yusuf ibn Sa'd (not Ibn Mahak), from Muhammad ibn Hatib, from 'Ali, and he mentioned it, and its wording is: "'Uthman is among them."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾: "Those are the friends of Allah who pass over the Path at a speed faster than lightning, while the disbelievers remain in it, kneeling."

This agrees with what we have mentioned. Others said: rather, it was revealed as an exception from those who were worshipped, and 'Uzayr and the Messiah were excluded from them, as Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war said, from Ibn Jurayj and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾, then he made an exception, saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾. It is said: they are the angels, 'Isa, and similar ones who are worshipped besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic. 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj also said likewise.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾: "It was revealed concerning 'Isa son of Maryam and 'Uzayr, peace be upon them both."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn 'Isa ibn Maysarah narrated to us, Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, Sa'd ibn Tarif narrated to us, from al-Asbagh, from 'Ali regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾, he said: "Everything that is worshipped besides Allah is in the Fire, except the sun, the moon, and 'Isa son of Maryam." Its chain is weak.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Those will be kept far from it﴾: "'Isa, 'Uzayr, and the angels."

Al-Dahhak said: "'Isa, Maryam, the angels, the sun, and the moon." Similarly it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, and more than one other.

Ibn Abi Hatim has narrated in this regard a very strange hadith. He said: al-Fadl ibn Ya'qub al-Rukhkhani narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Maslamah ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated to us, from Mughith, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾, he said: "'Isa, 'Uzayr, and the angels." [Its chain includes Sa'id ibn Maslamah and his teacher al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who are both weak.]

Some of them mentioned the story of Ibn al-Za'bari and the debate of the polytheists. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said:

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Anmati narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Hakim narrated to us, al-Hakam (i.e. Ibn Aban) narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "You claim that Allah revealed to you this verse: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to enter it﴾?" Ibn al-Za'bari said: "The sun, the moon, the angels, 'Uzayr and 'Isa son of Maryam have been worshipped. Are all these in the Fire along with our gods?" Then it was revealed: ﴿And when the son of Maryam is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it. And they say: "Are our gods better, or is he?" They do not cite him to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. Then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾. Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abdullah narrated it in his book "al-Ahadith al-Mukhtarah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Qabisah ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, Sufyan (i.e. al-Thawri) narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from his companions, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to enter it﴾, the polytheists said: "So the angels, 'Uzayr and 'Isa are worshipped besides Allah?" Then it was revealed: ﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it﴾, meaning the gods that are worshipped, ﴿And all will abide therein forever﴾.

It is also narrated from Abu Kudaynah, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same, and he said: then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾.

* *

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾: "Those are the friends of Allah who pass over the Path at a speed faster than lightning, while the disbelievers remain in it, kneeling."

This agrees with what we have mentioned. Others said: rather, it was revealed as an exception from those who were worshipped, and 'Uzayr and the Messiah were excluded from them, as Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war said, from Ibn Jurayj and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾, then he made an exception, saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾. It is said: they are the angels, 'Isa, and similar ones who are worshipped besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic. 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj also said likewise.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾: "It was revealed concerning 'Isa son of Maryam and 'Uzayr, peace be upon them both."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn 'Isa ibn Maysarah narrated to us, Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, Sa'd ibn Tarif narrated to us, from al-Asbagh, from 'Ali regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾, he said: "Everything that is worshipped besides Allah is in the Fire, except the sun, the moon, and 'Isa son of Maryam." Its chain is weak.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Those will be kept far from it﴾: "'Isa, 'Uzayr, and the angels."

Al-Dahhak said: "'Isa, Maryam, the angels, the sun, and the moon." Similarly it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, and more than one other.

Ibn Abi Hatim has narrated in this regard a very strange hadith. He said: al-Fadl ibn Ya'qub al-Rukhkhani narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Maslamah ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated to us, from Mughith, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾, he said: "'Isa, 'Uzayr, and the angels." [Its chain includes Sa'id ibn Maslamah and his teacher al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who are both weak.]

Some of them mentioned the story of Ibn al-Za'bari and the debate of the polytheists. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said:

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Anmati narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Hakim narrated to us, al-Hakam (i.e. Ibn Aban) narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "You claim that Allah revealed to you this verse: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to enter it﴾?" Ibn al-Za'bari said: "The sun, the moon, the angels, 'Uzayr and 'Isa son of Maryam have been worshipped. Are all these in the Fire along with our gods?" Then it was revealed: ﴿And when the son of Maryam is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it. And they say: "Are our gods better, or is he?" They do not cite him to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. Then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾. Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abdullah narrated it in his book "al-Ahadith al-Mukhtarah."

Then it was revealed: ﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it﴾, meaning the gods that are worshipped, ﴿And all will abide therein forever﴾.

It is also narrated from Abu Kudaynah, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same, and he said: then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith interrupted him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) argued with him until he silenced him, and he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to enter it﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And they therein will not hear﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari al-Sahmi came and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib just now, nor did he sit. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of these gods of ours are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have defeated him in argument. Ask Muhammad: everything that is worshipped besides Allah is in Hell along with those who worship it. We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship 'Isa son of Maryam. Are they too in Hell?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the assembly were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari, and they saw that he had argued and prevailed in dispute.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 21, verse 98–103 (part 2 of 2):

This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him. Indeed, they are only worshipping the devils (al-shayatin)[[In T and F: "al-shaytan".]] and whoever commanded them to worship him[[In F: "amarahum".]]." And Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) has already preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it. They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide in whatever their souls desire.﴾ That is: Jesus, Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped among the rabbis and monks, those who died upon the obedience of Allah, whereas those among the people of misguidance who worshipped them took them as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants. They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 26-29]. And it was revealed concerning what was mentioned about the matter of Jesus, and that he is worshipped besides Allah, and the amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is presented as an example, behold, your people turn away from it, and they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They do not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people. He is not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels upon the earth succeeding (one another). And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour, so do not be doubtful about it.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 57-61]. That is: the signs We placed upon his hands, such as reviving the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 61][[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358), and al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (17/76).]].

And what Ibn al-Zaba'ra said is a great error, because the verse was revealed as an address to the people of Makkah concerning their worship of idols, which are inanimate objects that do not understand, in order to rebuke and reproach their worshippers. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell.﴾ How then can Jesus, Uzayr, and similar ones, who had righteous deeds and did not approve of those who worshipped them, be included in this? Ibn Jarir, in his Tafsir, relied in his answer on the fact that "ma" (what) is used for that which does not understand, according to the Arabs.

Abdullah ibn al-Zaba'ra later embraced Islam, and he was one of the well-known poets. He had previously been satirizing the Muslims, then he said, apologizing:

O Messenger of the Sovereign, indeed my tongue
Has mended what I had torn, for I was ruined...
When I accompanied Satan on the paths of error,
And whoever inclines to his inclination is destroyed.[[The two verses are in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/419).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ It was said: the intended meaning is death. Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, from Yahya ibn Rabi'ah, from Ata'.

It was also said: the intended meaning of "the greatest terror" is the blast in the Trumpet. Said by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, and Abu Sinan Sa'id[[In T, F, A: "Sa'd".]] ibn Sinan al-Shaybani, and Ibn Jarir chose this in his Tafsir.

It was also said: when the servant is commanded to the Fire. Said by al-Hasan al-Basri.

It was also said: when the Fire closes over its people. Said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Juraij.

It was also said: when death is slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire. Said by Abu Bakr al-Hudhali[[In F, A: "al-Hamdani".]], as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the angels will meet them, saying, "This is your day which you were promised."﴾ He means: the angels will say to them, giving them good news on the Day of their return when they come out of their graves: ﴿This is your day which you were promised.﴾ That is: receive what will gladden you.

He (Allah) says, addressing the people of Makkah among the polytheists of Quraysh and those who followed their religion from among the worshippers of idols and images:

﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: that is, its fuel, as in His saying: ﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6].

Ibn 'Abbas also said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means the trees of Hell. In another narration he said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means the firewood of Hell, in the Zanji language (the language of the Zanj).

Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: its firewood. This is also how it is read in the qira'a (variant recitation) of 'Ali and 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means what is thrown into it.

Others said similarly. All these meanings are close to one another.

* *

His saying: ﴿You are to enter it﴾ means: you will enter it.

Al-zafir is the expulsion of their breaths, and al-shahiq is the drawing in of their breaths. ﴿And they therein will not hear﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman (i.e. al-Mas'udi) narrated to us, from his father, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: When there remain those who will abide forever in the Fire, they will be placed in coffins of fire, with nails of fire, so that none of them will see that anyone else is being punished in the Fire. Then 'Abdullah recited: ﴿For them therein is groaning, and they therein will not hear﴾.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from al-Mas'udi, from Yunus ibn Khabbab [in T: "Ibn Hibban"], from Ibn Mas'ud, and he mentioned it.

* *

When Allah mentioned the people of the Fire and their punishment because of their associating partners with Allah, He followed it with mention of the happy among the believers in Allah and His messengers [in T: "messenger"], those for whom happiness had preceded from Allah, and who sent forward righteous deeds in this world, as He said: ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26], and He said: ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60]. Just as they did good in this world, Allah made their end and their reward good, so He saved them from the punishment and granted them abundant reward. He said: ﴿Those will be kept far from it. They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that is, its burning in the bodies.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Jurayri [in T, F, A: "from Abu 'Uthman al-Jurayri"], from Abu 'Uthman, regarding ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, he said: there are serpents on the Path (al-Sirat) that sting them, and when they are stung, he says: "Hass, hass" [an exclamation of pain].

* *

Ibn 'Abbas also said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means the trees of Hell. In another narration he said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means the firewood of Hell, in the Zanji language (the language of the Zanj).

Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and Qatadah said: its firewood. This is also how it is read in the qira'a (variant recitation) of 'Ali and 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Al-Dahhak said: ﴿Ḥaṣab Jahannam﴾ means what is thrown into it.

Others said similarly. All these meanings are close to one another.

* *

His saying: ﴿You are to enter it﴾ means: you will enter it.

﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it﴾: that is, if these idols and rivals which you have taken besides Allah were true gods, they would not have entered the Fire, nor would they have gone into it. ﴿And all will abide therein forever﴾: that is, the worshippers and what they worshipped, all of them will abide in it forever. ﴿For them therein is groaning﴾, as He said: ﴿For them therein is groaning and wailing﴾ [Hud: 106]. Al-zafir is the expulsion of their breaths, and al-shahiq is the drawing in of their breaths. ﴿And they therein will not hear﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman (i.e. al-Mas'udi) narrated to us, from his father, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: When there remain those who will abide forever in the Fire, they will be placed in coffins of fire, with nails of fire, so that none of them will see that anyone else is being punished in the Fire. Then 'Abdullah recited: ﴿For them therein is groaning, and they therein will not hear﴾.

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, from al-Mas'udi, from Yunus ibn Khabbab [in T: "Ibn Hibban"], from Ibn Mas'ud, and he mentioned it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾: 'Ikrimah said: the mercy. Others said: the happiness. ﴿Those will be kept far from it﴾. When Allah mentioned the people of the Fire and their punishment because of their associating partners with Allah, He followed it with mention of the happy among the believers in Allah and His messengers [in T: "messenger"], those for whom happiness had preceded from Allah, and who sent forward righteous deeds in this world, as He said: ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and more﴾ [Yunus: 26], and He said: ﴿Is the reward for good anything but good?﴾ [al-Rahman: 60]. Just as they did good in this world, Allah made their end and their reward good, so He saved them from the punishment and granted them abundant reward. He said: ﴿Those will be kept far from it. They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, that is, its burning in the bodies.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from his father, from al-Jurayri [in T, F, A: "from Abu 'Uthman al-Jurayri"], from Abu 'Uthman, regarding ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾, he said: there are serpents on the Path (al-Sirat) that sting them, and when they are stung, he says: "Hass, hass" [an exclamation of pain].

* *

His saying: ﴿And they, in what their souls desire, will abide forever﴾: He saved them from what is feared and dreaded, and they obtained what is sought and loved.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Abi Suraj narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Abi Yazid al-Hamdani narrated to us, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from the paternal cousin of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: [he spent the night chatting with 'Ali one night, and he recited: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾, and he said: "I am among them, 'Umar is among them, 'Uthman is among them, al-Zubayr is among them, Talhah is among them, 'Abd al-Rahman is among them" or he said: "Sa'd is among them." He said: The prayer was established, so he stood up, and I think he was dragging his garment, and he was saying: ﴿They will not hear its faintest sound﴾.

Shu'bah said, from Abu Bishr, from Yusuf al-Makki, from Muhammad ibn Hatib [in T: "Khatib"], who said: I heard 'Ali say regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾: "'Uthman and his companions."

Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it, and Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Yusuf ibn Sa'd (not Ibn Mahak), from Muhammad ibn Hatib, from 'Ali, and he mentioned it, and its wording is: "'Uthman is among them."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾: "Those are the friends of Allah who pass over the Path at a speed faster than lightning, while the disbelievers remain in it, kneeling."

This agrees with what we have mentioned. Others said: rather, it was revealed as an exception from those who were worshipped, and 'Uzayr and the Messiah were excluded from them, as Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war said, from Ibn Jurayj and 'Uthman ibn 'Ata', from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell﴾, then he made an exception, saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾. It is said: they are the angels, 'Isa, and similar ones who are worshipped besides Allah, Mighty and Majestic. 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan and Ibn Jurayj also said likewise.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾: "It was revealed concerning 'Isa son of Maryam and 'Uzayr, peace be upon them both."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Husayn ibn 'Isa ibn Maysarah narrated to us, Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, Sa'd ibn Tarif narrated to us, from al-Asbagh, from 'Ali regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us﴾, he said: "Everything that is worshipped besides Allah is in the Fire, except the sun, the moon, and 'Isa son of Maryam." Its chain is weak.

Ibn Abi Najih said, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Those will be kept far from it﴾: "'Isa, 'Uzayr, and the angels."

Al-Dahhak said: "'Isa, Maryam, the angels, the sun, and the moon." Similarly it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, and more than one other.

Ibn Abi Hatim has narrated in this regard a very strange hadith. He said: al-Fadl ibn Ya'qub al-Rukhkhani narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Maslamah ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated to us, from Mughith, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾, he said: "'Isa, 'Uzayr, and the angels." [Its chain includes Sa'id ibn Maslamah and his teacher al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who are both weak.]

Some of them mentioned the story of Ibn al-Za'bari and the debate of the polytheists. Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh said:

Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Sahl narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Anmati narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ar'arah narrated to us, Yazid ibn Abi Hakim narrated to us, al-Hakam (i.e. Ibn Aban) narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "You claim that Allah revealed to you this verse: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to enter it﴾?" Ibn al-Za'bari said: "The sun, the moon, the angels, 'Uzayr and 'Isa son of Maryam have been worshipped. Are all these in the Fire along with our gods?" Then it was revealed: ﴿And when the son of Maryam is cited as an example, behold, your people turn away from it. And they say: "Are our gods better, or is he?" They do not cite him to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people﴾. Then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾. Al-Hafiz Abu 'Abdullah narrated it in his book "al-Ahadith al-Mukhtarah."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Qabisah ibn 'Uqbah narrated to us, Sufyan (i.e. al-Thawri) narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from his companions, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to enter it﴾, the polytheists said: "So the angels, 'Uzayr and 'Isa are worshipped besides Allah?" Then it was revealed: ﴿If these had been gods, they would not have entered it﴾, meaning the gods that are worshipped, ﴿And all will abide therein forever﴾.

It is also narrated from Abu Kudaynah, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same, and he said: then it was revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best reward has preceded from Us, those will be kept far from it﴾.

Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his book "al-Sirah": It is reported to me that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) once sat with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah in the mosque, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith came and sat with them, and in the mosque were more than one man of the men of Quraysh. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) spoke, and al-Nadr ibn al-Harith interrupted him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) argued with him until he silenced him, and he recited to him and to them: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are the fuel of Hell; you are to enter it﴾, up to His saying: ﴿And they therein will not hear﴾. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up, and 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari al-Sahmi came and sat down. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah said to 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari: "By Allah, al-Nadr ibn al-Harith did not stand up for the son of 'Abd al-Muttalib just now, nor did he sit. Muhammad claims that we and what we worship of these gods of ours are the fuel of Hell." 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari said: "By Allah, if I had found him, I would have defeated him in argument. Ask Muhammad: everything that is worshipped besides Allah is in Hell along with those who worship it. We worship the angels, the Jews worship 'Uzayr, and the Christians worship 'Isa son of Maryam. Are they too in Hell?" Al-Walid and those who were with him in the assembly were amazed at the words of 'Abdullah ibn al-Za'bari, and they saw that he had argued and prevailed in dispute.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 21, verse 98–103 (part 2 of 2):

This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him. Indeed, they are only worshipping the devils (al-shayatin)[[In T and F: "al-shaytan".]] and whoever commanded them to worship him[[In F: "amarahum".]]." And Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) has already preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it. They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide in whatever their souls desire.﴾ That is: Jesus, Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped among the rabbis and monks, those who died upon the obedience of Allah, whereas those among the people of misguidance who worshipped them took them as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants. They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 26-29]. And it was revealed concerning what was mentioned about the matter of Jesus, and that he is worshipped besides Allah, and the amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is presented as an example, behold, your people turn away from it, and they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They do not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people. He is not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels upon the earth succeeding (one another). And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour, so do not be doubtful about it.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 57-61]. That is: the signs We placed upon his hands, such as reviving the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 61][[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358), and al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (17/76).]].

And what Ibn al-Zaba'ra said is a great error, because the verse was revealed as an address to the people of Makkah concerning their worship of idols, which are inanimate objects that do not understand, in order to rebuke and reproach their worshippers. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell.﴾ How then can Jesus, Uzayr, and similar ones, who had righteous deeds and did not approve of those who worshipped them, be included in this? Ibn Jarir, in his Tafsir, relied in his answer on the fact that "ma" (what) is used for that which does not understand, according to the Arabs.

Abdullah ibn al-Zaba'ra later embraced Islam, and he was one of the well-known poets. He had previously been satirizing the Muslims, then he said, apologizing:

O Messenger of the Sovereign, indeed my tongue
Has mended what I had torn, for I was ruined...
When I accompanied Satan on the paths of error,
And whoever inclines to his inclination is destroyed.[[The two verses are in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/419).]]
