Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 21, verse 98–103 (part 2 of 2):

This was mentioned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Whoever loves to be worshipped besides Allah is with those who worshipped him. Indeed, they are only worshipping the devils (al-shayatin)[[In T and F: "al-shaytan".]] and whoever commanded them to worship him[[In F: "amarahum".]]." And Allah revealed: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best (reward) has already preceded from Us, they will be kept far from it. They will not hear its faintest sound, and they will abide in whatever their souls desire.﴾ That is: Jesus, Uzayr, and whoever was worshipped among the rabbis and monks, those who died upon the obedience of Allah, whereas those among the people of misguidance who worshipped them took them as lords besides Allah. And it was revealed concerning what they mention, that they worship the angels and that they are the daughters of Allah: ﴿And they say, "The Most Merciful has taken a son." Glory be to Him! Rather, they are honored servants. They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And whoever among them says, "Indeed, I am a god besides Him," then We will recompense him with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Anbiya: 26-29]. And it was revealed concerning what was mentioned about the matter of Jesus, and that he is worshipped besides Allah, and the amazement of al-Walid and those present at his argument and dispute: ﴿And when the son of Mary is presented as an example, behold, your people turn away from it, and they say, "Are our gods better, or is he?" They do not present it to you except for argument. Rather, they are a quarrelsome people. He is not but a servant upon whom We bestowed favor, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel. And if We willed, We could make from you angels upon the earth succeeding (one another). And indeed, he is a sign for the Hour, so do not be doubtful about it.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 57-61]. That is: the signs We placed upon his hands, such as reviving the dead and healing the sick, are sufficient as evidence of the Hour. He says: ﴿So do not be doubtful about it, and follow Me. This is a straight path.﴾ [az-Zukhruf: 61][[Al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (1/358), and al-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir (17/76).]].

And what Ibn al-Zaba'ra said is a great error, because the verse was revealed as an address to the people of Makkah concerning their worship of idols, which are inanimate objects that do not understand, in order to rebuke and reproach their worshippers. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell.﴾ How then can Jesus, Uzayr, and similar ones, who had righteous deeds and did not approve of those who worshipped them, be included in this? Ibn Jarir, in his Tafsir, relied in his answer on the fact that "ma" (what) is used for that which does not understand, according to the Arabs.

Abdullah ibn al-Zaba'ra later embraced Islam, and he was one of the well-known poets. He had previously been satirizing the Muslims, then he said, apologizing:

O Messenger of the Sovereign, indeed my tongue
Has mended what I had torn, for I was ruined...
When I accompanied Satan on the paths of error,
And whoever inclines to his inclination is destroyed.[[The two verses are in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah of Ibn Hisham (2/419).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them﴾ It was said: the intended meaning is death. Narrated by Abd al-Razzaq, from Yahya ibn Rabi'ah, from Ata'.

It was also said: the intended meaning of "the greatest terror" is the blast in the Trumpet. Said by al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, and Abu Sinan Sa'id[[In T, F, A: "Sa'd".]] ibn Sinan al-Shaybani, and Ibn Jarir chose this in his Tafsir.

It was also said: when the servant is commanded to the Fire. Said by al-Hasan al-Basri.

It was also said: when the Fire closes over its people. Said by Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Juraij.

It was also said: when death is slaughtered between Paradise and the Fire. Said by Abu Bakr al-Hudhali[[In F, A: "al-Hamdani".]], as narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim from him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And the angels will meet them, saying, "This is your day which you were promised."﴾ He means: the angels will say to them, giving them good news on the Day of their return when they come out of their graves: ﴿This is your day which you were promised.﴾ That is: receive what will gladden you.

He, exalted is He, says: This will take place on the Day of Resurrection, ﴿the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for writings﴾, as He, exalted, said: ﴿They did not measure God with His true measure, while the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glorified is He and exalted above what they associate with Him﴾ [al-Zumar: 67]. Al-Bukhari said:

Muqaddam ibn Muhammad narrated to us: my paternal uncle al-Qasim ibn Yahya narrated to me, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "Indeed Allah will seize the earths on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be in His right hand" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (7412).]].

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route, may Allah have mercy on him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Raqqi narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from Abu al-Wasil [[In manuscript T: "al-Mawasil".]], from Abu al-Malih al-Azdi [[In manuscript T: "al-Awdi".]], from Abu al-Jawza' al-Azdi, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Allah [[In manuscript T: "Ilayhi" (to Him).]] will fold the seven heavens with what is in them of creation and the seven earths with what is in them of creation; He will fold all of that [[In manuscript F: "kulluhu dhalika".]] in His right hand, and all of it will be in His hand like a mustard seed.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿like the rolling up of the scroll for writings﴾, it has been said: the word "al-sijill" here means "the book." It has also been said that "al-sijill" here means: an angel from among the angels.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to us; Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us; Abu al-Wafa' al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Umar regarding His saying: ﴿the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for writings﴾, who said: "al-Sijill is an angel; when he ascends with the seeking of forgiveness, he says: Write it as light."

Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way, from Abu Kurayb, from Ibn Yaman, with the same chain.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It was also narrated from Abu Ja'far [[In manuscript T: "Abi Hafs".]] Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn that al-Sijill is an angel.

Al-Suddi said regarding this verse: "al-Sijill is an angel appointed over the pages. When a person dies, his book is raised to al-Sijill, who rolls it up and keeps it raised until the Day of Resurrection."

It has also been said that it refers to the name of a male companion who used to write down the revelation for the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us; Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us; Nuh ibn Qays narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding: [﴿the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for writings﴾] [[Addition from manuscript F.]], who said: "al-Sijill: he is a man."

Nuh said: Yazid ibn Ka'b [he is al-'Awdhi] informed me, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Sijill was a scribe [[In manuscript T: "kanat" (feminine form).]] of the Prophet ﷺ."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i narrated it in the same way, from Qutaybah ibn Sa'id [[In manuscript T: "Sa'd".]], from Nuh ibn Qays, from Yazid ibn Ka'b, from 'Amr ibn Malik, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "al-Sijill was a scribe [[In manuscript T: "kanat".]] of the Prophet ﷺ" [[Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (2935), and al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Nasa'i, no. (11335).]].

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Nasr ibn 'Ali al-Jahdami, as has preceded. Ibn 'Adi narrated it through the narration of Yahya ibn 'Amr ibn Malik al-Nukri, from his father, from Abu al-Jawza', from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Prophet [[In manuscript T: "There was for the Messenger of Allah".]] ﷺ had a scribe called [[In manuscript T: "was called".]] al-Sijill," and this is His saying: ﴿the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for writings﴾, meaning: just as the scroll folds the writing, so We fold the heaven. Then he said: "It is not preserved" [[al-Kamil (7/205).]].

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said in his History: Abu Bakr al-Barqani informed us; Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Hajjaji informed us; Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Karkhi informed us, that Hamdan ibn Sa'id narrated to them, from 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "al-Sijill: a scribe of the Prophet ﷺ" [[Tarikh Baghdad (8/175).]].

This is extremely munkar (rejected, a narration that is weak and contradicts reliable reports) in the hadith of Nafi' from Ibn 'Umar, and it is not authentic at all. Likewise, what preceded from Ibn 'Abbas through the narration of Abu Dawud and others is also not authentic. A group of the hadith memorizers have declared it fabricated, even though it is in the Sunan of Abu Dawud, among them our shaykh, the great hadith master Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, may Allah prolong his life, extend his lifespan, and conclude his life with righteous deeds. I have devoted a separate part to this hadith, and praise be to Allah. The Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir took up the rejection of this hadith and refuted it most thoroughly, and he said: "No one among the Companions is known by the name al-Sijill; the scribes of the Prophet ﷺ are well known, and none of them is named al-Sijill." He was truthful, may Allah have mercy on him, in this, and it is among the strongest evidences for the rejection of this hadith. As for those who mentioned this name among the Companions, they relied only on this hadith and nothing else, and Allah knows best.

The authentic report from Ibn 'Abbas is that al-Sijill is al-Sahifah (the page), as stated by 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah and al-'Awfi, from him. Mujahid, Qatadah, and others explicitly affirmed this. Ibn Jarir chose it, because it is the known meaning in the language. According to this, the meaning of the statement is: ﴿the Day We roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for writings﴾, i.e., upon [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]] the writing, in the sense of the written, like His saying: ﴿So when they had both submitted and he had laid him down upon his forehead﴾ [al-Saffat: 103], i.e., upon the forehead. There are similar usages in the language, and Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it, a promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing it﴾, it means: this will certainly happen, on the Day when Allah recreates the creatures in a new creation, just as He originated them. He is capable of restoring them, and this is bound to occur, because it is among the promises of Allah which are not broken and not changed, and He is capable of that. For this reason He said: ﴿indeed We are ever doing it﴾.

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' and Ibn Ja'far narrated to us, in meaning [[In manuscripts H, T, F, A: "Ibn Ja'far and 'Affan, in meaning"; the reading adopted is from the Musnad.]], and they both said [[In manuscript T: "They said".]]: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood among us giving an admonition and said: "Indeed you will be gathered to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, barefoot, naked, and uncircumcised, ﴿as We began the first creation, We will repeat it, a promise upon Us; indeed We are ever doing it﴾." He mentioned the rest of the hadith. Both of them [al-Bukhari and Muslim] narrated it in their Sahihs through the hadith of Shu'bah. Al-Bukhari also narrated it under this verse in his book [[Musnad (1/235); Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (4625), (4740); Sahih Muslim, no. (2860).]].

Al-Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated from Mujahid, from 'A'ishah, from the Prophet ﷺ, something similar to this.

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿As We began the first creation, We will repeat it﴾: "He said: We will destroy everything, just as it was the first time."

He, exalted is He, says, informing of what He decreed and determined for His righteous servants: happiness in this world and the Hereafter, and inheritance of the earth in this world and the Hereafter. This is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 128] And He said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand.﴾ [Ghafir: 51] And He said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, just as He granted succession to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely change [their state] after their fear into security [and He will replace them after their fear with security]﴾ [An-Nur: 55], and the verse [continues].

He informed, exalted is He, that this is written and inscribed in the scriptural (shar'iyyah) and the predestined (qadariyyah) books, so it will certainly come to pass. For this reason He said: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur after the Dhikr [that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants].﴾ Al-A'mash said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about His saying: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur after the Dhikr﴾, and he said: "The Zabur is the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an." [In A: "al-Furqan".]

Mujahid said: "The Zabur is the Book."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others said: "The Zabur is what was revealed to Dawud (David), and the Dhikr is the Torah." And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Zabur is the Qur'an."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The Dhikr is that which is in the heaven."

Mujahid said: "The Zabur is the books after the Dhikr, and the Dhikr is Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book) with Allah."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, preferred this view. [Tafsir al-Tabari (17/81).] Likewise Zayd ibn Aslam said: "It is the first Book." Al-Thawri said: "It is al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet)." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "The Zabur is the books that were sent down to the prophets, and the Dhikr is Umm al-Kitab, in which things are written before that."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Allah, glorified is He, informed in the Torah, the Zabur, and His foreknowledge before the heavens and the earth were created, that He would give the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) the earth and admit them into Paradise, and they are the righteous."

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾: "It is the earth of Paradise." Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Abu Salih, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and al-Thawri [may Allah have mercy on them all].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, meaning: indeed, in this Qur'an which We sent down upon Our servant Muhammad (ﷺ) is a message (balagh): benefit and sufficiency for a people who worship, and they are those who worship Allah by what He has legislated, loved, and approved, and who prefer obedience to Allah over obedience to Satan and the desires of their souls.

* *

As for His saying [exalted is He] [In T: "mighty and majestic"]: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾: He, exalted is He, informs that Allah made Muhammad (ﷺ) a mercy to the worlds, meaning: He sent him as a mercy to all of them. Whoever accepts this mercy and thanks for this blessing will be happy in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever rejects and denies it will lose in this world and the Hereafter, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the house of destruction — Hell, which they will burn in, and wretched is the place of settlement?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28-29]. And Allah, exalted is He, said describing the Qur'an: ﴿Say, "It is for those who believe a guidance and healing. And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. They are those who are called from a distant place."﴾ [Fussilat: 44]

Muslim said in his Sahih: Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Marwan al-Fazari narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, invoke curse upon the polytheists." He said: "I was not sent as one who curses, but I was sent only as a mercy." Muslim alone narrated it. [Sahih Muslim no. (2599).]

And in another hadith: "I am only a mercy presented as a gift." Narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn Abi 'Arabah and others, from Waki', from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, raised [to the Prophet (ﷺ)]. [Narrated by Abu al-Hasan al-Sukkari in al-Fawa'id al-Muntaqah (2/157), as in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah (1/803) by al-Albani.] Ibrahim al-Harbi said: "Others have narrated it from Waki' without mentioning Abu Hurayrah." [Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (11/504) narrated it from Waki' as mursal (missing the companion), and Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat (1/182) narrated it from Waki' as mursal.] Likewise said al-Bukhari when he was asked about this hadith; he said: "It was with Hafs ibn Ghiyath as mursal."

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir said: "It was also narrated by Malik ibn Su'ayr ibn al-Khims, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, raised." [Al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (2369) and al-Bayhaqi (1/158).] Then he related it through Abu Bakr ibn al-Muqri' and Abu Ahmad al-Hakim, both from Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sufi: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, from Abu Usamah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays [In T and A: "Hasan".] ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am only a mercy presented as a gift."

Then he cited it through al-Salt ibn Mas'ud, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Mis'ar [In A: "from Shu'bah"], from Sa'id ibn Khalid, from a man, from Ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah sent me as a mercy presented as a gift; I was sent to elevate a people and to lower others." [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Jami' al-Saghir, and al-Albani graded it as weak.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nafi' al-Tahhan narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: I found a book in Madinah from 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Darawardi and Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from Muhammad ibn Salih al-Tammar, from Ibn [Shihab] [In A: added], from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father who said: Abu Jahl said when he came to [Makkah] [In A: added] returning from [his confrontation with] Hamzah: "O assembly of Quraysh, indeed Muhammad has descended upon Yathrib and sent out his advance guards, and he only wants to strike something from you. So beware of passing his path or approaching him [In T: "or fighting him"], for he is like a ravenous lion. He is angry with you because you expelled him as lice are expelled from the hooves [In A: "people"]. By Allah, he has sorcery; I have never seen him nor any of his companions except that I saw Satan with them. You know the enmity of the two sons of Qaylah — meaning the Aws and the Khazraj — they are an enemy who sought help from an enemy." Muti' ibn 'Adiyy said to him: "O Abu al-Hakam, by Allah, I have not seen anyone more truthful in speech nor more faithful to a promise than your brother whom you expelled. Since you have done what you did, be the most restrained of people from him." [Abu Sufyan] [In A: added] ibn al-Harith said: "Be as hostile as you have ever been to him. The two sons of Qaylah, if they overcome you, will not spare you any kinship or covenant. If you obey me, you will force them to a worse sorrow, or you will expel Muhammad from among them, and he will be alone and driven out. As for the two sons of Qaylah, by Allah, they and the people of Dahlak [In T and A: added] are equal in humiliation." And he said:

"I will give a harsh side of myself ... despite what was of closeness and distance ..."

"The men of the Khazrajiyyah are a people of humiliation ... whenever jest follows earnestness."

When this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, I will surely kill them, crucify them, and guide them, while they are unwilling. Indeed I am a mercy whom Allah sent. Allah will not take me away until He makes His religion prevail. I have five names: I am Muhammad, Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser), by whom Allah erases disbelief; I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer), upon whose footsteps people will be gathered; and I am al-'Aqib (the Successor)." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/123).]

Ahmad ibn Salih said: "I hope the hadith is sound."

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Qays narrated to me, from 'Amr ibn Abi Qurrah al-Kindi who said: Hudhayfah was at al-Mada'in, and he would mention things that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said. Hudhayfah came to Salman, and Salman said: "O Hudhayfah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would become angry and say something, and become pleased and say something. I know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave a sermon and said: 'Any man of my community whom I insult in my anger, or whom I curse with a curse, I am only a man from the children of Adam; I become angry as they become angry. Indeed Allah sent me only as a mercy to the worlds. So make that a means of prayer for him on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it from Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Za'idah. [Musnad (5/437) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4659).]

If it is said: "What mercy did one who disbelieved in him receive?" The answer is what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir narrated: Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to us, Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from a man called Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾, he said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, mercy is written for him in this world and the Hereafter; and whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger is protected from what befell the nations of earthquake and stoning." [Tafsir al-Tabari (17/83).]

Similarly Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of al-Mas'udi, from Abu Sa'd — who is Sa'id ibn al-Marzuban al-Baqqal — from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned it in similar wording. And Allah knows best.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani also narrated it from 'Abdan ibn Ahmad, from 'Isa ibn Yunus al-Ramli, from Ayyub ibn Suwayd, from al-Mas'udi, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾, he said: "Whoever follows him, it will be a mercy for him in this world and the Hereafter; and whoever does not follow him is protected from what all the other nations were afflicted with of earthquake and stoning." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/23).]

He, exalted is He, says, informing of what He decreed and determined for His righteous servants: happiness in this world and the Hereafter, and inheritance of the earth in this world and the Hereafter. This is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 128] And He said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand.﴾ [Ghafir: 51] And He said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, just as He granted succession to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely change [their state] after their fear into security [and He will replace them after their fear with security]﴾ [An-Nur: 55], and the verse [continues].

He informed, exalted is He, that this is written and inscribed in the scriptural (shar'iyyah) and the predestined (qadariyyah) books, so it will certainly come to pass. For this reason He said: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur after the Dhikr [that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants].﴾ Al-A'mash said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about His saying: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur after the Dhikr﴾, and he said: "The Zabur is the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an." [In A: "al-Furqan".]

Mujahid said: "The Zabur is the Book."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others said: "The Zabur is what was revealed to Dawud (David), and the Dhikr is the Torah." And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Zabur is the Qur'an."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The Dhikr is that which is in the heaven."

Mujahid said: "The Zabur is the books after the Dhikr, and the Dhikr is Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book) with Allah."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, preferred this view. [Tafsir al-Tabari (17/81).] Likewise Zayd ibn Aslam said: "It is the first Book." Al-Thawri said: "It is al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet)." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "The Zabur is the books that were sent down to the prophets, and the Dhikr is Umm al-Kitab, in which things are written before that."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "Allah, glorified is He, informed in the Torah, the Zabur, and His foreknowledge before the heavens and the earth were created, that He would give the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) the earth and admit them into Paradise, and they are the righteous."

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾: "It is the earth of Paradise." Likewise said Abu al-'Aliyah, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, al-Suddi, Abu Salih, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and al-Thawri [may Allah have mercy on them all].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾, meaning: indeed, in this Qur'an which We sent down upon Our servant Muhammad (ﷺ) is a message (balagh): benefit and sufficiency for a people who worship, and they are those who worship Allah by what He has legislated, loved, and approved, and who prefer obedience to Allah over obedience to Satan and the desires of their souls.

* *

As for His saying [exalted is He] [In T: "mighty and majestic"]: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾: He, exalted is He, informs that Allah made Muhammad (ﷺ) a mercy to the worlds, meaning: He sent him as a mercy to all of them. Whoever accepts this mercy and thanks for this blessing will be happy in this world and the Hereafter, and whoever rejects and denies it will lose in this world and the Hereafter, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to settle in the house of destruction — Hell, which they will burn in, and wretched is the place of settlement?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28-29]. And Allah, exalted is He, said describing the Qur'an: ﴿Say, "It is for those who believe a guidance and healing. And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them. They are those who are called from a distant place."﴾ [Fussilat: 44]

Muslim said in his Sahih: Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Marwan al-Fazari narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Kaysan, from Ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, invoke curse upon the polytheists." He said: "I was not sent as one who curses, but I was sent only as a mercy." Muslim alone narrated it. [Sahih Muslim no. (2599).]

And in another hadith: "I am only a mercy presented as a gift." Narrated by 'Abd Allah ibn Abi 'Arabah and others, from Waki', from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, raised [to the Prophet (ﷺ)]. [Narrated by Abu al-Hasan al-Sukkari in al-Fawa'id al-Muntaqah (2/157), as in al-Silsilah al-Sahihah (1/803) by al-Albani.] Ibrahim al-Harbi said: "Others have narrated it from Waki' without mentioning Abu Hurayrah." [Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf (11/504) narrated it from Waki' as mursal (missing the companion), and Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat (1/182) narrated it from Waki' as mursal.] Likewise said al-Bukhari when he was asked about this hadith; he said: "It was with Hafs ibn Ghiyath as mursal."

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir said: "It was also narrated by Malik ibn Su'ayr ibn al-Khims, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, raised." [Al-Bazzar in his Musnad no. (2369) and al-Bayhaqi (1/158).] Then he related it through Abu Bakr ibn al-Muqri' and Abu Ahmad al-Hakim, both from Bakr ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Sufi: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, from Abu Usamah, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays [In T and A: "Hasan".] ibn Abi Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I am only a mercy presented as a gift."

Then he cited it through al-Salt ibn Mas'ud, from Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Mis'ar [In A: "from Shu'bah"], from Sa'id ibn Khalid, from a man, from Ibn 'Umar who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah sent me as a mercy presented as a gift; I was sent to elevate a people and to lower others." [Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Jami' al-Saghir, and al-Albani graded it as weak.]

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nafi' al-Tahhan narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: I found a book in Madinah from 'Abd al-'Aziz al-Darawardi and Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, from Muhammad ibn Salih al-Tammar, from Ibn [Shihab] [In A: added], from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father who said: Abu Jahl said when he came to [Makkah] [In A: added] returning from [his confrontation with] Hamzah: "O assembly of Quraysh, indeed Muhammad has descended upon Yathrib and sent out his advance guards, and he only wants to strike something from you. So beware of passing his path or approaching him [In T: "or fighting him"], for he is like a ravenous lion. He is angry with you because you expelled him as lice are expelled from the hooves [In A: "people"]. By Allah, he has sorcery; I have never seen him nor any of his companions except that I saw Satan with them. You know the enmity of the two sons of Qaylah — meaning the Aws and the Khazraj — they are an enemy who sought help from an enemy." Muti' ibn 'Adiyy said to him: "O Abu al-Hakam, by Allah, I have not seen anyone more truthful in speech nor more faithful to a promise than your brother whom you expelled. Since you have done what you did, be the most restrained of people from him." [Abu Sufyan] [In A: added] ibn al-Harith said: "Be as hostile as you have ever been to him. The two sons of Qaylah, if they overcome you, will not spare you any kinship or covenant. If you obey me, you will force them to a worse sorrow, or you will expel Muhammad from among them, and he will be alone and driven out. As for the two sons of Qaylah, by Allah, they and the people of Dahlak [In T and A: added] are equal in humiliation." And he said:

"I will give a harsh side of myself ... despite what was of closeness and distance ..."

"The men of the Khazrajiyyah are a people of humiliation ... whenever jest follows earnestness."

When this reached the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, I will surely kill them, crucify them, and guide them, while they are unwilling. Indeed I am a mercy whom Allah sent. Allah will not take me away until He makes His religion prevail. I have five names: I am Muhammad, Ahmad, I am al-Mahi (the Eraser), by whom Allah erases disbelief; I am al-Hashir (the Gatherer), upon whose footsteps people will be gathered; and I am al-'Aqib (the Successor)." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/123).]

Ahmad ibn Salih said: "I hope the hadith is sound."

Imam Ahmad said: Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us, Za'idah narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Qays narrated to me, from 'Amr ibn Abi Qurrah al-Kindi who said: Hudhayfah was at al-Mada'in, and he would mention things that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said. Hudhayfah came to Salman, and Salman said: "O Hudhayfah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would become angry and say something, and become pleased and say something. I know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave a sermon and said: 'Any man of my community whom I insult in my anger, or whom I curse with a curse, I am only a man from the children of Adam; I become angry as they become angry. Indeed Allah sent me only as a mercy to the worlds. So make that a means of prayer for him on the Day of Resurrection.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it from Ahmad ibn Yunus, from Za'idah. [Musnad (5/437) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4659).]

If it is said: "What mercy did one who disbelieved in him receive?" The answer is what Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir narrated: Ishaq ibn Shahin narrated to us, Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from a man called Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾, he said: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, mercy is written for him in this world and the Hereafter; and whoever does not believe in Allah and His Messenger is protected from what befell the nations of earthquake and stoning." [Tafsir al-Tabari (17/83).]

Similarly Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of al-Mas'udi, from Abu Sa'd — who is Sa'id ibn al-Marzuban al-Baqqal — from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, and he mentioned it in similar wording. And Allah knows best.

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani also narrated it from 'Abdan ibn Ahmad, from 'Isa ibn Yunus al-Ramli, from Ayyub ibn Suwayd, from al-Mas'udi, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾, he said: "Whoever follows him, it will be a mercy for him in this world and the Hereafter; and whoever does not follow him is protected from what all the other nations were afflicted with of earthquake and stoning." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12/23).]

He, exalted is He, says, informing of what He decreed and determined for His righteous servants: happiness in this world and the Hereafter, and inheritance of the earth in this world and the Hereafter. This is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 128] And He said: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand.﴾ [Ghafir: 51] And He said: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, just as He granted succession to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely change [their state] after their fear into security [and He will replace them after their fear with security]﴾ [An-Nur: 55], and the verse [continues].

He informed, exalted is He, that this is written and inscribed in the scriptural (shar'iyyah) and the predestined (qadariyyah) books, so it will certainly come to pass. For this reason He said: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur after the Dhikr [that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants].﴾ Al-A'mash said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about His saying: ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur after the Dhikr﴾, and he said: "The Zabur is the Torah, the Gospel, and the Qur'an." [In A: "al-Furqan".]

Mujahid said: "The Zabur is the Book."

Ibn 'Abbas, al-Sha'bi, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and others said: "The Zabur is what was revealed to Dawud (David), and the Dhikr is the Torah." And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: "The Zabur is the Qur'an."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The Dhikr is that which is in the heaven."

Mujahid said: "The Zabur is the books after the Dhikr, and the Dhikr is Umm al-Kitab (the Mother of the Book) with Allah."

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari), may Allah have mercy on him, preferred this view. [Tafsir al-Tabari (17/81).] Likewise Zayd ibn Aslam said: "It is the first Book." Al-Thawri said: "It is al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (the Preserved Tablet)." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "The Zabur is the books that were sent down to the prophets, and the Dhikr is Umm al-Kitab, in which things are written before that."

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, to say to the polytheists: ﴿Say: "It is only revealed to me that your God is one God, so will you submit?"﴾ That is: will you follow this, submit and yield to Him?

﴿But if they turn away﴾ that is, they abandon what you call them to, ﴿then say: "I have informed you upon equal terms."﴾ That is: I have made known to you that I am at war with you just as you are at war with me, I am free of you just as you are free of me. This is like His saying: ﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my deed, and for you is your deed. You are free of what I do, and I am free of what you do."﴾ [Yunus: 41]. And He said: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their covenant] upon equal terms﴾ [al-Anfal: 58]: let your knowledge and theirs of the abrogation of the covenants be on equal terms. Likewise here: ﴿But if they turn away, say: "I have informed you upon equal terms"﴾ that is: I have made known to you my disassociation from you and your disassociation from me, knowing this.

* *

His saying: ﴿And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾ that is: it will certainly occur, but I have no knowledge of whether it is near or far. ﴿Indeed, He knows what is spoken openly and He knows what you conceal﴾ that is: Allah knows all of the unseen, and He knows what the servants display and what they keep secret. He knows the outward and the inward, and He knows the secret and what is more hidden, and He knows what the servants do openly and secretly, and He will recompense them for that, for the small and the great.

* *

His saying: ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and a provision for a time.﴾ That is: I do not know whether this is a trial for you and a provision for a time.

Ibn Jarir said: "Perhaps the delay of that from you is a trial for you, and a provision until a specified term." And Awn related it from Ibn Abbas. And Allah knows best.

﴿He said: "My Lord, judge with truth."﴾ That is: decide between us and our people who deny the truth.

Qatadah said: The prophets, peace be upon them, used to say: ﴿Our Lord, decide between us and our people with truth, and You are the best of deciders﴾ [al-A'raf: 89], and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was commanded to say that.

And from Malik, from Zayd ibn Aslam: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ witnessed battle, he would say: ﴿My Lord, judge with truth.﴾

* *
